# Components

Every component with all kits enabled. Each entry: name and summary, then one line per prop (name, type, description), its `parts`, and whether it takes `children`. Core built-ins come first, then `ui-*` (ui-kit), `ui-chart` / `ui-sparkline` / `ui-live-data` (chart-kit), `ui-flow*` (flow-kit), `ui-map*` (map-kit), `ui-twin*` (twin-kit) and `ui-icon` (icon-kit).

```
element: Any HTML element. Set attributes with `attrs`.
  tag          tag  HTML tag name (default `div`)
  children: yes
text: Text content.
  value        any (required)  The text. Templates update live when they use `state`.
  tag          tag  HTML tag (default `span`), e.g. `h1`, `p`, `li`
  children: no
stack: Flex layout container.
  direction    one of: row, column, row-reverse, column-reverse  Default `column`
  gap          any  Number (px, following the theme's `space.scale` and `space.gap`), CSS length or `$token`
  align        any  `align-items`
  justify      any  `justify-content`
  wrap         bool  Wrap children onto multiple lines
  tag          tag  HTML tag (default `div`)
  children: yes
button: A button. Wire it up with `on.click`.
  label        any  Button text, rendered in the `label` part
  variant      one of: primary, secondary, ghost  Default `primary`
  type         one of: button, submit, reset  Default `button`
  disabled     any  Boolean or expression
  parts: label
  children: yes
input: Form input.
  bind         statekey  State key kept in sync with the value (`checked` for checkboxes)
  type         string  Input type (default `text`)
  placeholder  any  
  name         string  Form field name (bound radios default to the `bind` key)
  value        any  Initial value when not bound; for a bound radio, the value it stands for
  disabled     any  Boolean or expression
  children: no
select: Dropdown.
  options      any (required)  Array of values or `{ value, label, disabled }`. Rebuilt in the browser when it uses state.
  bind         statekey  State key kept in sync with the selected value (a list of them with `multiple`)
  multiple     bool  Several can be picked (a list box; Ctrl or ⌘ and a click, Shift for a run); the key holds a list
  placeholder  any  Text of a first, empty option (not with `multiple`)
  name         string  Form field name
  value        any  Initially selected value when not bound
  disabled     any  Boolean or expression
  children: no
textarea: Multi-line text input.
  bind         statekey  State key kept in sync with the text
  placeholder  any  
  name         string  Form field name
  rows         any  Visible lines (default 3)
  value        any  Initial text when not bound
  disabled     any  Boolean or expression
  children: no
list: Renders its children once per item. Rebuilt in the browser when `items` uses state.
  items        any (required)  An array: `{{ data.path }}`, or `{{ state_key }}` to rebuild in the browser
  as           string  Name of the current item (default `item`)
  index        string  Name of the current index (default `index`)
  tag          tag  HTML tag (default `div`), e.g. `ul`
  key          any  Per-item key, e.g. `{{ item.id }}`. When the browser rebuilds the list, items whose key survives keep their nodes
  children: yes
if: Renders its children when `when` is truthy. Adds no element of its own. A following `else` (with `when` for else-if) renders when it doesn't.
  when         any (required)  Condition. Shown and hidden in the browser when it uses state.
  children: yes
ui-button: A button in six variants and four sizes. With `href` it is a link that looks like a button.
  label        any  Button text
  icon         any  An icon name (with the icon kit) or a character, before the label
  variant      one of: default, secondary, destructive, outline, ghost, link, brand  Default `default`
  size         one of: default, sm, lg, icon  Default `default`
  href         any  Render a link that looks like a button
  type         one of: button, submit, reset  Default `button`
  disabled     any  Boolean or expression
  children: yes
ui-camera: Takes photos: front and back camera, light, zoom, composing lines, a timer, retakes and several shots, made smaller before they're kept. Where there's no camera to use, the device's own picker.
  bind         statekey (required)  State key for the photo, `{ id, url, name, type, size, width, height, at }` (`url` is a `data:` address), or with `multiple` a list of them
  multiple     bool  Several photos
  max          number  At most this many
  facing       one of: back, front  The camera it starts with (default `back`)
  ratio        any  The photo's shape, e.g. `1` or `"4 / 3"` (default the camera's)
  maxSize      number  The photo's longer side at most, in px (default 1600)
  quality      number  0 to 1 (default 0.8)
  type         one of: jpeg, webp, png  Default `jpeg`
  review       bool  Each photo is looked at first, to use or retake (default true, or false with `multiple`)
  grid         bool  Lines for composing start shown
  timer        number  Seconds between the button and the photo (default 0)
  guide        one of: none, card, face, square  An outline to fill
  stamp        any  Written along the foot of the photo, e.g. `{{ site }} · {{ now }}`; `time` is the date and time
  files        bool  Photos can be chosen from the device too (default true)
  autoStart    bool  The camera starts by itself, where it's been allowed
  label        any  The button that starts it (default `Open the camera`)
  disabled     any  Shown, not changed
  children: no
ui-permission-manager: What the app may use (camera, location, notifications…): why, whether it's allowed, a button to ask, and how to allow what was blocked.
  permissions  any (required)  What's used: names, or `{ name, label, reason, required }`: `camera`, `microphone`, `geolocation`, `notifications`, `motion`, `storage` (kept when space is short), `clipboard` or `nfc`
  bind         statekey  State key that gets each one's answer, e.g. `{ camera: granted, geolocation: prompt }`: `granted`, `denied`, `prompt` or `unsupported`
  bindReady    statekey  State key that's true once every one that's `required` is allowed
  title        any  Over them
  children: no
ui-photo-annotate: Marks on a photo: arrows, boxes, circles, freehand, text, measurements and blurring (for faces and number plates), kept apart from the picture and drawn onto a copy of it.
  src          any (required)  The picture: an address or `data:`; may use state. An object with a `url` (a `ui-camera` photo) will do
  bind         statekey  State key that gets the picture with the marks drawn on it (a `data:` address) as they change
  bindMarks    statekey  State key for the marks: `[{ id, type, points, text, color }]`, points as parts of the picture, 0 to 1
  tools        any  Which, in order: `[select, arrow, box, circle, pen, text, measure, blur]` (default all)
  colors       any  Default red, amber, green, blue, white and black
  width        number  Of the lines, in px of a 1000 px wide picture (default 6)
  unit         any  For measurements, e.g. `cm`: the first one's length is typed, and the others are worked out from it (default `cm`)
  type         one of: jpeg, png, webp  Default `jpeg`
  quality      number  0 to 1 (default 0.85)
  maxSize      number  The result's longer side at most, in px (default 2000)
  readonly     bool  The marks are shown, not changed
  label        any  Names it (default `Mark up the photo`)
  children: no
ui-location: Where the device is, once or as it moves, with how accurate that is; typed instead where it can't be found.
  bind         statekey (required)  State key that gets `{ lat, lng, accuracy, altitude, heading, speed, at }`, the accuracy in metres
  watch        bool  Follows the device as it moves, while the page is open
  auto         bool  Found by itself, where it's been allowed
  precise      bool  With GPS rather than a quick guess (default true)
  enough       number  Metres: keeps trying for a while until it's as accurate as this
  manual       bool  Can be typed instead
  link         any  Where its Open in maps goes, with `{lat}` and `{lng}` (default OpenStreetMap); null for none
  label        any  The button (default `Use my location`)
  children: no
ui-field-map: A light map to move and zoom, drawn without a library: markers (grouped when they're close), areas, lines, where the device is, and drawing on it.
  center       any  `{ lat, lng }` or `[lat, lng]`; may use state, and the map follows it (default: what's on it)
  zoom         any  0 (the world) to 19 (a building); may use state
  markers      any  `[{ id, lat, lng, label, text, color, glyph }]`: `text` is shown when it's picked, `glyph` is a character in the pin
  areas        any  `[{ id, points: [[lat, lng]], label, color }]`, or a circle: `{ lat, lng, radius }`, in metres
  lines        any  `[{ id, points, color, width, dashed, label }]`
  cluster      bool  Markers near each other are one, with their number, until zoomed in
  bindSelected statekey  State key for the id of the marker, area or line picked
  bindView     statekey  State key that gets `{ lat, lng, zoom, bounds: [[south, west], [north, east]] }` as it's moved
  bindPoint    statekey  State key that gets `{ lat, lng }` where the map was clicked
  bindDrawn    statekey  State key for what's drawn on it: `[{ id, type, points, radius }]`
  draw         any  What can be drawn: `[marker, line, polygon, circle]`
  locate       bool  A button shows where the device is
  position     any  A dot at `{ lat, lng, accuracy, heading }`, e.g. what `ui-location` gives
  fit          bool  Starts with everything on it in view (default true, without `center`)
  height       any  Default 360 px
  tiles        any  Tiles' address, with `{z}`, `{x}` and `{y}`; `none` for a plain ground (default OpenStreetMap's, which are for light use: name your own for an app)
  attribution  any  Whose map it is (default `© OpenStreetMap contributors`)
  darkTiles    bool  In dark mode the tiles are turned dark (default true)
  wheel        bool  The wheel zooms without Ctrl or ⌘
  minZoom      number  Default 1
  maxZoom      number  Default 19
  label        any  Names it for screen readers (default `Map`)
  children: no
ui-geo-checkin: Checks in and out where someone has to be: how far they are from the place, the time, how long it's been, and a photo. Children (a `ui-camera`, say) go before the button. A device can be made to lie about where it is, so it's a record, not proof.
  bind         statekey (required)  State key for the visit that's open, `{ id, place, in: { at, lat, lng, accuracy, distance, inside, reason, photo } }` (null when there's none)
  places       any (required)  Where one can check in: `[{ id, name, lat, lng, radius }]`, metres, or `points` for an area; may use state
  bindLog      statekey  State key that collects the visits that have ended, with `out` and `seconds`
  outside      one of: block, reason, allow  Away from every place: not at all (default), with a reason, or allowed
  enough       number  The least accuracy that counts, in metres (default 100)
  ready        any  The button waits for this, e.g. `{{ photo != null }}`
  photo        any  Kept with it, e.g. `{{ photo }}`
  inLabel      any  Default `Check in`
  outLabel     any  Default `Check out`
  children: yes
ui-route-tracker: Records a path while the app is open and in front: distance, time and speed, with pause, and GPX to save. Draw it on a `ui-field-map`, and keep it with `ui-local-store`.
  bind         statekey (required)  State key for the route, `{ state: idle|recording|paused|done, points: [[lat, lng, time, accuracy]], distance, seconds, started, ended }`, metres
  step         number  Metres between points at least (default 10)
  enough       number  Points less accurate than this are left out, in metres (default 50)
  units        one of: metric, imperial  Default `metric`
  awake        bool  Keeps the screen on while it records (default true): a phone stops saying where it is once it sleeps
  download     string  A button saves it as GPX under this name, e.g. `route.gpx`
  children: no
ui-compass: Which way the device faces, and the way to a place from where one is. A phone's magnet is easily put off by metal.
  bind         statekey  State key that gets the heading, degrees from north
  heading      any  Or shown from this, e.g. a vehicle's or the wind's
  target       any  `{ lat, lng }` to point to, from `from`
  from         any  Where one is, e.g. what `ui-location` gives
  size         number  In px (default 220)
  children: no
ui-level: A spirit level from the device's own sensors, set to zero against a surface known to be level.
  bind         statekey  State key that gets `{ x, y, level }`, degrees off level
  value        any  Or shown from this `{ x, y }`
  tolerance    number  Degrees that count as level (default 0.5)
  mode         one of: surface, edge, auto  Lying on a surface, stood on an edge, or whichever it is (default `auto`)
  size         number  In px (default 220)
  children: no
ui-push-opt-in: Offers notifications at a good moment, says why, then asks; subscribes to pushes and sends the subscription to a server, by topic. The app's service worker (`irender app`) shows them.
  publicKey    any  The server's VAPID public key; without it, only the app's own notifications are allowed for, with no pushes
  saveUrl      any  The subscription and topics are POSTed here as JSON, `{ subscription, topics }`, and again as they change; `subscription` is null once they're off
  topics       any  What can be chosen: `[{ value, label, description, on }]`
  bind         statekey  State key that gets `{ state, topics, endpoint }`; `state`: on, off, denied, install (an iPhone, until the app's on the home screen) or unsupported
  title        any  Default `Stay up to date`
  text         any  Why, before the browser asks
  label        any  The button (default `Turn on notifications`)
  when         any  Waits for a good moment, e.g. `{{ ordered }}`: shown once this is true
  remember     string  A Not now button, which keeps it away for `days` in this browser, under this name
  days         number  Default 30
  test         bool  Once on, a button shows one
  children: no
ui-app-badge: A number on the installed app's icon, and in the tab's title. Draws nothing.
  count        any (required)  The number; none at 0, and a dot for `true`; may use state
  title        bool  Before the page's title too, as `(3) Inbox` (default true)
  children: no
ui-share: Shares a link, text or files with the device's own sheet; where there's none, a list: copy, email, download and others.
  url          any  A link (default the page's when there's nothing else); may use state
  title        any  May use state
  text         any  May use state
  files        any  Files to share: `[{ url, name, type }]`, e.g. `ui-camera` photos; may use state
  label        any  Default `Share`
  variant      one of: primary, outline, ghost  Default `outline`
  targets      any  Besides copying and email, where there's no share sheet: `[{ label, href }]`, with `{url}`, `{title}` and `{text}` in `href`
  sheet        one of: auto, own  `own` always shows the list, not the device's sheet (default `auto`)
  children: no
ui-share-target: Takes what other apps share with this one, once it's installed: put it on the page that the document's `app.share` names.
  bind         statekey (required)  State key that gets what was shared: `{ title, text, url, files: [{ name, type, size, url }], at }`
  quiet        bool  Draws nothing
  acceptLabel  any  Default `Add it`; runs `on: { accept: … }`
  emptyText    any  Shown while nothing has been
  children: no
ui-contact-picker: Contacts picked from the phone's own list (Chrome on Android); anywhere else, from a contact card file (.vcf) or typed.
  bind         statekey (required)  State key for the contact, `{ name, tel: [], email: [] }`, or with `multiple` a list of them
  multiple     bool  Several
  fields       any  What's asked for: `[name, tel, email, address]` (default the first three)
  manual       bool  Can be typed (default true)
  label        any  Default `Choose a contact`
  children: no
ui-passkey: Signs in, or makes the passkey to, with a fingerprint, a face or the device's PIN. The server makes the challenge and checks the answer.
  mode         one of: signin, register  Default `signin`
  optionsUrl   any  POSTed `body` for the server's options (WebAuthn's, as JSON)
  verifyUrl    any  POSTed the passkey's answer as JSON; what it replies goes to `bind`
  body         any  Sent for the options, e.g. `{ email: "{{ email }}" }`
  bind         statekey  State key that gets the server's reply
  autofill     bool  Offered among the browser's suggestions for a field with `autocomplete: username webauthn`
  local        bool  Without a server, for this device only: it shows someone can unlock the device, and proves nothing to a server
  name         any  With `local`, what it's called
  label        any  Default `Sign in with a passkey`, or `Create a passkey`
  variant      one of: primary, outline  Default `outline`
  children: no
ui-app-lock: Covers the app after a while, or once it's been out of sight, until it's opened with a passkey or a PIN. It keeps someone who picks up the device out; it doesn't encrypt anything, and a server still has to check who's asking.
  methods      any  How it's opened: `[passkey, pin]` (default both, as the device can)
  after        number  Minutes without anything done until it locks (default 5; 0: never)
  hidden       number  Seconds out of sight until it locks (default 30; 0: at once)
  digits       number  Of the PIN, 4 to 8 (default 4)
  tries        number  Wrong PINs before it makes one wait, longer each time (default 5)
  name         string  Kept under this name on the device (default `app`)
  bindLocked   statekey  State key that's true while it's locked, e.g. to take things off the page
  title        any  Default `Locked`
  logo         any  A picture's address, over the title
  signOutUrl   any  Where `Forgot your PIN?` goes, after the `forgot` event; it stays locked until `reset`
  reset        any  Takes the lock off, e.g. once they've signed in again: `{{ signedInNow }}`
  settings     bool  Draws turning it on and off, changing the PIN and locking now (default true)
  children: no
ui-audio-recorder: Voice notes: records with a moving waveform, pauses, plays back and goes to any point of it.
  bind         statekey (required)  State key for the recording, `{ id, url, name, type, size, seconds, peaks, at }` (`url` is a `data:` address), or with `multiple` a list of them
  multiple     bool  Several
  max          number  Seconds at most (default 300)
  bitrate      number  Bits a second (default 48000, good for voice)
  label        any  Default `Record`
  disabled     any  Played, not changed
  children: no
ui-video-recorder: Records a short video with a time limit, pauses, and plays it back to keep or take again.
  bind         statekey (required)  State key for the video, `{ id, url, name, type, size, seconds, at }` (`url` is a `data:` address)
  max          number  Seconds at most (default 30)
  facing       one of: front, back  Default `front`
  audio        bool  With sound (default true)
  bitrate      number  Bits a second (default 1200000)
  height       number  Of the video in px (default 720)
  label        any  Default `Open the camera`
  disabled     any  Played, not changed
  children: no
ui-screen-capture: A picture or a video of a screen, a window or a tab, which someone picks: for reporting a problem, say. Phones can't.
  bind         statekey (required)  State key for what's taken: a picture `{ id, url, name, type, size, width, height, at }`, or a video
  modes        any  `[picture, video]` (default both)
  max          number  Seconds of video at most (default 60)
  audio        bool  With the sound of what's shared, where it can be
  children: no
ui-voice-input: Speech to text, shown as it's heard. Some browsers send what's said to their maker's servers to do it.
  bind         statekey (required)  State key for the text
  append       bool  After what's there already (default true)
  continuous   bool  Goes on past a pause, until it's stopped
  lang         any  What's spoken, e.g. `en-GB` (default the document's)
  transcribeUrl any  Where the browser can't (Firefox), what's said is recorded and POSTed here as `audio`; the reply is `{ text }`
  iconOnly     bool  Only a microphone, for beside a field
  label        any  Default `Speak`
  children: no
ui-read-aloud: Reads text, or a part of the page, out loud with the device's own voices, with pause and speed.
  text         any  What's read; may use state
  target       string  Or a part of the page, a CSS selector: each sentence is marked as it's read
  lang         any  Default the document's
  voice        any  A voice's name, or the start of it
  rate         number  0.5 to 2 (default 1)
  controls     bool  Speed can be changed
  bindState    statekey  State key that gets `playing`, `paused` or `stopped`
  label        any  Default `Read aloud`
  children: no
ui-wake-lock: Keeps the screen on: a recipe, a score, a boarding pass, a timer.
  active       any  The screen's kept on while this is true, e.g. `{{ step > 0 }}`
  bind         statekey  Or a state key, with a switch for it
  label        any  The switch's (default `Keep the screen on`)
  bindHeld     statekey  State key that's true while it's really kept on
  children: no
ui-swipe-actions: A row that's swiped sideways to show what can be done with it: archive, delete, call. Its children are the row.
  start        any  Under its start, shown by swiping that way: `[{ value, label, tone, icon }]`; each runs `on: { <value>: … }`
  end          any  Under its end
  full         bool  Swiping all the way runs the outermost one (default true)
  menu         bool  A button shows them too, for a mouse and the keyboard (default true)
  label        any  Names the row in that button, e.g. `{{ m.from }}`
  disabled     any  Doesn't swipe
  parts: content
  children: yes
ui-document-scanner: Scans papers with the camera or from a picture: finds the page's edges, straightens it, cleans it up, and makes a PDF of several.
  bind         statekey (required)  State key for the pages: `[{ id, url, width, height }]`, each a `data:` picture
  bindPdf      statekey  State key that gets them as one PDF, `{ url, name, type, size, pages }`
  max          number  Pages at most
  filter       one of: colour, grey, bw, none  How it starts: brightened, grey, black and white, or as it was (default `colour`)
  paper        one of: auto, a4, letter  The PDF's pages (default `auto`: each picture's shape)
  maxSize      number  A page's longer side at most, in px (default 1800)
  quality      number  0 to 1 (default 0.75)
  name         any  The PDF's name (default `scan.pdf`)
  label        any  Default `Scan a page`
  children: no
ui-nfc: Reads NFC tags held to the phone, and writes to them (Chrome on Android).
  bind         statekey (required)  State key that gets the last tag read, `{ serial, records: [{ type, text }], text, at }`
  bindList     statekey  State key that collects each different tag
  write        any  Text or an address to write, with a button for it; may use state
  lock         bool  What's written can't be changed again, ever
  label        any  Default `Read a tag`
  children: no
ui-bluetooth: Connects to a Bluetooth Low Energy device, reads and follows its values, and sends to it (Chrome and Edge; not iPhones).
  read         any (required)  What's read: `[{ key, service, characteristic, as, notify, label, unit }]`, by name (`battery_service`) or number; `as`: uint8 (default), int8, uint16, int16, uint32, float32, text, hex or heart-rate; `scale`, `offset`
  bind         statekey  State key that gets the values by `key`
  bindState    statekey  State key that gets `disconnected`, `connecting` or `connected`
  commands     any  Buttons that write: `[{ label, service, characteristic, value, as }]`; `value` may use state
  namePrefix   string  Only devices whose name starts with this are listed
  label        any  Default `Connect a device`
  children: no
ui-serial: Talks to a serial port, a line at a time: scales, meters, microcontrollers (Chrome and Edge on a computer).
  baud         number  Default 9600
  bind         statekey  State key that gets the last line, read by `parse`
  bindLog      statekey  State key that gets the last lines, `[{ at, text, out }]`
  bindState    statekey  State key that gets `disconnected`, `connecting` or `connected`
  parse        one of: text, number, json, csv  What a line is (default `text`); `number` is the first one in it
  end          one of: lf, crlf, cr, none  Ends what's sent (default `lf`)
  filters      any  Only these are listed: `[{ usbVendorId, usbProductId }]`
  send         bool  A field to send lines with
  commands     any  Buttons that send: `[{ label, text }]`; `text` may use state
  log          bool  Shows the lines (default true)
  max          number  Lines kept (default 200)
  label        any  Default `Connect a port`
  children: no
ui-usb: Talks to a USB device that no driver has taken: label printers, scanners, instruments (Chrome and Edge).
  filters      any (required)  Which devices are listed: `[{ vendorId, productId, classCode }]`
  bind         statekey  State key that gets what's read last, by `as`
  bindState    statekey  State key that gets `disconnected`, `connecting` or `connected`
  bindDevice   statekey  State key that gets `{ name, maker, serial, vendorId, productId }`
  interface    number  Its number (default the first that can be used)
  as           one of: text, hex, bytes  What's read and sent are (default `text`)
  commands     any  Buttons that send: `[{ label, value }]`; `value` may use state
  label        any  Default `Connect a device`
  children: no
ui-file-handler: Opens files, from a button or, installed, when one's opened with the app (the document's `app.files`), and saves back to them.
  bind         statekey (required)  State key that gets the file opened: `{ name, type, size, text }`, or `url` (a `data:` address) or `json` for another `as`
  as           one of: text, json, data  Default `text`
  accept       any  Types and their endings: `{ text/markdown: [.md] }`
  save         any  What Save writes, to the file that was opened where the browser can, else as a new one; may use state
  name         any  A new file's name
  bindDirty    statekey  State key that's true while `save` isn't what's in the file
  label        any  Default `Open a file`
  children: no
ui-install-prompt: Offers to install the app: the browser's own prompt where there is one, else the steps for this browser (on an iPhone, Add to Home Screen). Hidden in the installed app. Needs the document's `app`.
  variant      one of: button, card, floating  Default `button`; `floating` is a card at the foot of the window
  label        any  The button (default `Install the app`)
  title        any  On the card (default the app's name)
  text         any  Under it (default `Opens from your home screen, and works offline.`)
  icon         any  A picture's address, on the card
  bindState    statekey  State key that gets `available` (the browser can install it), `steps` (it's added from a menu, which the button explains), `installed` or `unavailable`
  remember     string  A card has a Not now button, and once that's pressed stays away for `days` in this browser, under this name
  days         number  Default 30
  always       bool  Shown wherever it is, with the steps where there's no prompt
  children: no
ui-update-prompt: Says when a new version of the app has been fetched, and reloads into it when asked. `reload` comes first, for saving what's open.
  title        any  Default `A new version is ready`
  text         any  Under it, e.g. what's new
  label        any  The button (default `Reload`)
  laterLabel   any  Default `Later`; null for none
  every        number  Minutes between looking for one, besides each time the app's opened (default 60)
  inline       bool  In the page rather than at the foot of the window
  show         any  Shown whether there's one or not, e.g. when the host says
  bind         statekey  State key that's true while a new version is waiting
  children: no
ui-offline-indicator: Whether there's a connection: a badge, a banner or a dot, and state for the rest of the page.
  bind         statekey  State key that gets `online`, `offline` or `reconnecting`
  variant      one of: badge, banner, dot, none  Default `badge`; `none` only keeps the state
  showOnline   bool  Shown when there's a connection too
  checkUrl     any  Asked while there's doubt, as a device can be on a network that goes nowhere
  every        number  Seconds between those (default 15)
  offlineText  any  Default `Offline`
  onlineText   any  Default `Online`
  reconnectingText any  Default `Reconnecting…`
  detail       any  After it in a banner, e.g. `What you do is kept and sent later.`
  children: no
ui-offline-queue: Keeps what's sent without a connection (submits, forms and uploads) and sends it once there is one, in order, even after the app's been closed. Shows what's waiting and what was refused. Each is sent with an `x-queued-id` header, so a server can tell one it has had.
  paths        any  Addresses whose requests are kept, e.g. `[/api/inspections]`: any under them (default every one on the site)
  methods      any  Default `[POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE]`
  labels       any  What to call them: `{ /api/inspections: Inspection }`
  labelField   string  A field of what's sent that says which, e.g. `title`
  variant      one of: list, badge, none  Default `list`
  bind         statekey  State key that gets what's waiting: `[{ id, label, url, method, at, status, error, tries }]`
  bindCount    statekey  State key that gets how many
  retryEvery   number  Seconds between tries while the page is open (default 60)
  title        any  Over the list (default `Waiting to be sent`)
  emptyText    any  Default `Everything has been sent`
  hideEmpty    bool  Nothing is shown when there's nothing waiting
  children: no
ui-local-store: Keeps state keys on the device between visits. Draws nothing. Not for secrets: anyone with the device can read them.
  keys         any (required)  State keys to keep, e.g. `[draft, filters]`
  name         string  What they're kept under (default the page's address)
  where        one of: device, session  `device` (default) until cleared, `session` until the tab's closed
  maxAge       number  Days after which they're let go (default never)
  version      any  What's kept under another one is let go
  sync         bool  Other tabs follow (default true)
  bindReady    statekey  State key that's true once what was kept has been put back
  bindSaved    statekey  State key that gets the time they were last kept
  clear        any  When this becomes true, what's kept is let go
  children: no
ui-data-source: Says how one kind of record is fetched by id (people, items, accounts), for `expand` on tables and queries. Ids asked for together are fetched together, each once, and kept in memory for `ttl`. Draws nothing.
  name         string (required)  What queries and tables call it in `expand`, e.g. `people`
  key          string  The field that holds a record's id (default `id`)
  batch        any  Many ids in one call: `{ url, method, param, style, params, body, max, pick }`. GET (default) sends `<url>?ids=1,2,3` (`param` names it; `style: repeat` sends `ids=1&ids=2`); POST sends `{ ids: [...] }` with `body`'s fields. At most `max` ids a call (default 50). The answer is a list of records or a map by id, at `pick` (default the answer, or its `rows`, `data` or `items`)
  one          string  One id a call, where there's no `batch`: GET `<url>` with `{id}` in it, e.g. `/api/people/{id}`; 404 means there's none
  pick         string  With `one`: the record's path in the answer, e.g. `data`
  ttl          number  Seconds a record is kept before it's fetched again (default 300); it's shown meanwhile
  missingTtl   number  Seconds an id with no record is remembered as none before it's asked for again (default `ttl`)
  concurrency  number  Calls at a time (default 4)
  wait         number  Milliseconds to gather ids before calling (default 0: what's asked for in the same turn)
  headers      any  Request headers, e.g. `{ x-tenant: acme }`
  persist      one of: memory, device  `memory` (default): for the page's life; `device`: kept on the device too (IndexedDB), shown first and when offline
  scope        any  With `device`: whose records these are, e.g. `{{ user.id }}`; another one lets the others go from the page, and they're kept apart
  private      any  Fields kept on the device only encrypted, with the key a `ui-app-lock` unlocks (none: they aren't kept), e.g. `[email, phone]`
  retain       number  Days private fields may stay on the device without being fetched again (default 30)
  clear        any  When this becomes true, its records (of `scope`, or every one without) are let go from the device and the page, e.g. `{{ !user }}`
  write        any  Changes made here, also offline: `{ url, create, method, version, conflict }`. A `submit` to `url` (`/api/people/{id}`: PATCH, PUT or POST changes, DELETE deletes) or `create` (POST) changes the record at once and is sent when there's a connection, with the version it was made on: `If-Match` with the record's ETag (`version: etag`, default), or a field (`version: version`) sent in the body too. A 409 or 412 is settled by `conflict`: `merge` (default: both sides' changes, asking only about a field both changed), `server-wins`, `client-wins` or `ask`
  bindWrites   statekey  State key that gets this source's changes not yet saved: `[{ id, record, kind, status, error, changes, fields }]`, status waiting, sending, conflict or refused
  children: no
ui-data-query: Fills a state key with rows from an API, or with records by id, joined to the records they name (`expand`), for a chart, a list or any component. The rows come first; joined fields follow as their records arrive. Draws nothing.
  into         statekey (required)  State key that gets the rows (or the record, for one id)
  url          any  GET this for the rows; may use state, and a change loads again. The answer is a list, `{ rows, total }`, or one record
  params       any  Query parameters for `url`; blank ones are left out, and a change loads again
  pick         string  Path to the rows in the answer (default the answer, or its `rows`, `data` or `items`)
  source       string  Instead of `url`: the records of this `ui-data-source` for `ids`
  ids          any  With `source`: an id (into gets the record) or a list (the records); may use state
  expand       any  Joins records into each row: `{ owner: { source: people, from: ownerId } }` puts the `people` record whose id is in `ownerId` in `owner` (`from` may hold a list of ids). While it's on its way the row's `$loading.owner` is true; `$failed.owner` when it couldn't be fetched
  status       statekey  State key that gets `{ state, pending, total, error, at }`: state is idle, loading, joining (rows here, joined records on their way), ready or error
  refresh      any  Loads again when this changes, e.g. `{{ saved }}`
  paused       any  Nothing is loaded while true
  headers      any  Request headers for `url`
  persist      one of: memory, device  `memory` (default): for the page's life; `device`: kept on the device too (IndexedDB), shown first and when offline
  scope        any  With `device`: whose records these are, e.g. `{{ user.id }}`; another one lets the others go from the page, and they're kept apart
  private      any  Fields kept on the device only encrypted, with the key a `ui-app-lock` unlocks (none: they aren't kept), e.g. `[email, phone]`
  retain       number  Days private fields may stay on the device without being fetched again (default 30)
  sync         any  Asks only for what changed since the last answer: `true` or `{ param, cursor, deleted, tombstone, key, full }`. The answer's `cursor` (default `cursor`) is sent back as `?since=` (`param`); its rows replace those with the same `key` (default `id`) or are added, and rows whose `tombstone` field (default `deleted`) is true, or whose ids are in its `deleted` list, go. Everything is loaded again every `full` hours (default 24)
  every        number  Seconds between loads while the page is in sight (at least 5); it also loads when the connection comes back
  clear        any  When this becomes true, the answers kept for `scope` are let go and the rows emptied, and nothing loads while it stays true, e.g. `{{ !user }}`
  children: no
ui-data-conflicts: Changes made here that the server changed too, to settle field by field (yours or theirs), and changes it refused, to dismiss: for a `ui-data-source` with `write` and `conflict: ask` (or a field both changed with `merge`).
  source       string  Only this `ui-data-source`'s (default every one's)

  nameField    string  The record's field that names it, e.g. `name` (default its id)
  title        any  Default `Changed by someone else`
  emptyText    any  Shown when there's nothing to settle (default: it hides)
  children: no

ui-file-upload: Files to attach: a drop zone, uploads with progress, the files as a grid or a list, a preview of images, PDFs, spreadsheets and text, and Download all as a zip. The files are kept in state under `bind`.
  bind         statekey (required)  State key for the files: `[{ id, name, size, type, url, status, progress, error }]`. Files already there (with a `url`) are shown too
  url          any  Where to upload: each file is POSTed as `multipart/form-data` (field `file`), and a JSON answer is merged into its entry, e.g. `{ id, url }`. Without it, files stay in the browser
  params       any  More form fields sent with each file, e.g. `{ folder: "{{ claim.id }}" }`
  accept       string  Types allowed, as the file input's `accept`: `image/*,.pdf,.xlsx`
  multiple     bool  More than one file (default true)
  maxFiles     number  Most files in all
  maxSize      any  Largest file: bytes, or text like `10 MB` or `500 KB`
  view         one of: grid, list  `grid` of cards (default) or `list` of rows
  label        any  The drop zone's text (default `Drop files here or click to browse`)
  hint         any  Smaller text under it, e.g. the types and size allowed
  readOnly     bool  Show the files only: no drop zone and no removing
  removable    bool  A remove button on each file (default true)
  download     bool  A Download all button that saves the files as one zip (default true)
  zipName      string  The zip's name, without `.zip` (default `attachments`)
  emptyText    any  Shown under a read-only list with no files (default `No files yet.`)
  disabled     any  Boolean or expression
  id           any  The file input's id, for a label (default: derived from the document)
  parts: zone, files
  children: no
ui-status-badge: A status in its colour: common ones (Done, Paid, Open, In review, Blocked, Overdue, …) know theirs, and `tones` sets the rest.
  status       any (required)  The status, e.g. `In review` or `{{ ticket.status }}`
  tones        any  Status → tone (`neutral`, `info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `primary`), over the built-in ones, e.g. `{ Shipped: success }`
  labels       any  Status → text to show, e.g. `{ in_progress: In progress }` (default: the status)
  dot          bool  A dot before the text (default true)
  children: no
ui-progress-ring: A circular progress with the value in the middle.
  value        any (required)  0–100. Follows state when it uses it, e.g. `{{ project.done }}`
  size         number  Width and height in px (default 48)
  thickness    number  The ring's width in px (default: a tenth of the size)
  text         any  In the middle (default: the value with `%`); empty for none
  label        any  What it measures, for screen readers, e.g. `Project progress`
  tone         one of: neutral, info, success, warning, danger, primary  Its colour (default `primary`)
  children: no
ui-gauge: A figure on a dial from `min` to `max`, with coloured bands, a target and a needle; follows state without a script.
  value        any (required)  The figure. Follows state when it uses it, e.g. `{{ line.oee }}`
  min          number  The dial's start (default 0)
  max          number  The dial's end (default 100)
  unit         any  After the figure, smaller, e.g. `%` or `°C`
  text         any  In the middle in place of the value, e.g. a formatted one; empty for none
  decimals     number  The figure rounded to this many decimals, 0–10 (also when it follows state)
  ticks        number  Marks dividing the dial into this many equal parts, 2–20
  bands        any  Coloured stretches of the dial, in order: `{ to, tone, label }`, the last without `to` running to `max`. The value takes the tone of the band it's in
  tone         one of: neutral, info, success, warning, danger, primary  The value's colour (default: its band's, else `primary`)
  target       any  A mark across the dial at this value; may use state
  needle       bool  A needle pointing at the value, as well as the arc
  shape        one of: arc, half  `arc` (default, 240°) or `half` (a semicircle)
  size         number  Width in px (default 160)
  thickness    number  The dial's width in px (default: a twelfth of the size)
  scale        bool  `min` and `max` at the dial's ends (default true)
  caption      any  Text under the dial, e.g. what it measures
  label        any  What it measures, for screen readers (default: `caption`)
  children: no
ui-sortable-list: A list in state put in order by dragging each item's grip, or from the keyboard; children are each item's content, with `item` and `index` in scope.
  bind         statekey (required)  State key holding the list, in order: plain values or objects
  itemKey      string  With objects, the field that tells them apart (default `id`)
  labelField   string  With objects, the field shown and read out for each (default `label`)
  numbered     bool  Each item's place before it: 1, 2, 3
  removable    bool  A button on each item that takes it out of the list
  emptyText    any  Shown while the list is empty (default `Nothing here yet`)
  label        any  Names the list for screen readers (default `List`)
  disabled     any  Boolean or expression: no moving or removing
  id           any  Element id (default: derived from the document)
  children: yes
ui-form-builder: A form put together in the browser: field types added from a palette, put in order, set up in an inspector, tried in a preview, and given out as an iRender document of the kit's own form.
  bind         statekey (required)  State key holding the fields, in order: `{ id, type, label, description, placeholder, required, options, min, max, minLength, maxLength, pattern, patternMessage, when }`; `when: { field, value }` shows it only when that earlier field has that answer
  bindDocument statekey  State key that gets the form as an iRender document, kept up to date
  types        any  The field types offered, from `text`, `textarea`, `email`, `number`, `date`, `select`, `radio`, `checkboxes`, `checkbox`, `section` (default all)
  submitLabel  any  The generated form's submit button (default `Submit`)
  endpoint     string  Where the generated form posts its answers (as JSON); without it, the form thanks the person instead
  label        any  Names the builder for screen readers (default `Form builder`)
  id           any  Element id (default: derived from the document)
  children: no
ui-countdown: The time left to a deadline, turning to warning and danger as thresholds pass and counting up once overdue; as text or tiles, with a bar of the time used.
  to           any (required)  The deadline: a date and time (`2026-12-01T17:00`, `2026-12-01T17:00:00Z`), milliseconds, or `+7h 40m` from when the page opens; may use state
  from         any  When the time started, as `to` (`-16h 20m`: before the page opened): a bar shows how much of it is used
  warn         any  Time left when it turns to the warning tone: seconds, or `90s`, `30m`, `4h`, `2d`
  danger       any  Time left when it turns to the danger tone, as `warn`
  overdue      bool  Past the deadline, count up as overdue (default true); false shows `endText`
  endText      any  Shown once it's over, with `overdue: false` (default `Time's up`)
  format       one of: units, clock  `units` (default: `2d 4h`, `13m 05s`) or `clock` (`2:04:13`, `3d 02:04:13`)
  variant      one of: inline, tiles  `inline` (default: text with a dot in its tone) or `tiles` (days, hours, minutes and seconds in boxes)
  paused       any  While true (e.g. `{{ ticket.status == 'waiting' }}`), the time left stands still and it says Paused; on resuming the deadline moves out by the pause. A new `to` from the page replaces the moved one
  workdays     any  Count working time only: `true` for Monday to Friday, or the weekdays that work (0 is Sunday), e.g. `[0, 1, 2, 3, 4]`
  hours        any  Working hours each working day, e.g. `09:00-17:30` (local time); outside them it stands still. Alone, every day works
  holidays     any  Dates that don't count either, e.g. `["2026-12-25"]`
  bindLeft     statekey  State key that gets the seconds left (below zero once overdue), every second
  bindStatus   statekey  State key that gets `ok`, `warning`, `danger` or `over` as it changes
  label        any  What it counts down to, for screen readers, e.g. `First reply due`
  children: no
ui-iframe: Another page shown inside this one: sandboxed, loaded as it nears the screen, at a height or a ratio.
  src          any (required)  The page's address; may use state
  title        any  Names the frame for screen readers (default `Embedded page`)
  height       any  Number (px) or CSS length (default 400); ignored with `ratio`
  ratio        any  Width / height instead of a height: `"16 / 9"`, `1.5`
  sandbox      any  What the page may do: a list from `scripts`, `same-origin`, `forms`, `popups`, `popups-to-escape-sandbox`, `modals`, `downloads`, `presentation`, `pointer-lock`, `orientation-lock`, `top-navigation-by-user-activation`, `storage-access-by-user-activation`; `[]` for nothing, `false` for no sandbox (default `[scripts, same-origin, forms, popups, popups-to-escape-sandbox]`)
  allow        any  Browser features it may use: a list like `[fullscreen, clipboard-write, camera]`, or the `allow` attribute's text (default `[fullscreen]`)
  loading      one of: lazy, eager  Default `lazy`: loaded as it nears the screen
  referrerPolicy any  Default `strict-origin-when-cross-origin`
  bordered     bool  A border and rounded corners (default true)
  children: no
ui-compare-slider: Two pictures, before and after, one over the other, with a divider dragged across (or moved with the keys) to show more of either.
  before       any (required)  The first picture's address
  after        any (required)  The second picture's address, the same size and framing
  beforeAlt    any  What the first picture shows, for screen readers
  afterAlt     any  What the second picture shows, for screen readers
  beforeLabel  any  On the first picture's side (default `Before`); empty for none
  afterLabel   any  On the second picture's side (default `After`); empty for none
  position     number  Where the divider starts, 0–100 from the first side (default 50)
  bind         statekey  State key holding the divider's place, 0–100, both ways
  orientation  one of: horizontal, vertical  `horizontal` (default: the divider moves left and right) or `vertical` (up and down)
  hover        bool  The divider follows a mouse without pressing
  ratio        any  Width to height, e.g. `16/9` or `1`: both pictures fill it, cropped (default: the first picture's own)
  caption      any  Text under the pictures
  label        any  Names the comparison for screen readers (default `Before and after`)
  children: no
ui-presence: Who's here now: stacked avatars with a status dot and a colour each, then `+3`; a click lists everyone, their status and what they're on.
  people       any (required)  Who's here: `{ id, name, avatar, initials, status, color, where }`; `status` is active, idle, busy, away or offline, `color` 1–8 (default: by place), `where` what they're on. From state, it follows
  max          number  Avatars shown before `+3` (default 4)
  size         number  Avatar size in px (default 28)
  me           any  The `id` of whoever's looking: `(you)` after their name
  announce     bool  Say who joins and leaves, for screen readers
  align        one of: start, end  The list's edge lined up with the avatars (default `end`)
  label        any  What it shows (default `People here`)
  id           any  Element id (default: derived from the document)
  parts: trigger, popover
  children: no
ui-virtual-list: A long list that keeps only the items in view in the page, so thousands scroll smoothly; children are each item, with `item` and `index` in scope.
  items        any (required)  The items: a list, usually from state (`{{ rows }}`); it follows
  itemKey      string  The field that tells items apart (default `id`, else their place)
  height       any  The scrolling area's height: px or a CSS length (default 400)
  itemHeight   number  An item's height in px to start from, before items are measured (default 40)
  gap          number  Space between items in px (default 0)
  bindRange    statekey  State key that gets the places in view, `{ from, to, total }`, as it scrolls
  endThreshold number  How many items from the end `end` fires, to load more (default 10)
  emptyText    any  Shown while there are no items (default `Nothing to show`)
  label        any  Names the list for screen readers
  children: yes
ui-file-browser: Folders and files to browse one folder at a time, as a grid or a list: search, sort, select, rename, new folders, delete with undo, and move by dragging or a menu.
  bind         statekey (required)  State key holding the files and folders, a flat list: `{ id, name, parent, folder, size, modified, thumb, url }`; `parent` is the folder's `id` (none: the top), `folder: true` for a folder
  bindFolder   statekey  State key holding the open folder's `id` (null: the top), both ways
  url          string  Load a folder's contents when it's first opened: `GET <url>?folder=<id>` (no `folder` for the top) answering a list of items; they're added to `bind`
  uploadUrl    string  Files dropped from the desktop go up here, one `POST` each (form data `file` and `folder`), into the folder they're dropped on; an answer of an item takes the file's place
  bindSelection statekey  State key that gets the `id`s selected
  bindOpen     statekey  State key that gets the file opened (a double click, or Enter); `open` fires too
  view         one of: grid, list  How the folder shows to start with (default `grid`); a button switches
  editable     bool  New folders, renaming, deleting and moving (default true)
  rootLabel    any  The top folder's name in the breadcrumb (default `Files`)
  height       any  The files' area's height: px or a CSS length (default: as tall as they are)
  locale       string  How dates and sizes are written (default: the document's `lang`)
  label        any  Names it for screen readers (default `Files`)
  id           any  Element id (default: derived from the document)
  children: no
ui-approval: A sign-off in stages, each approved when its rule is met: who decided what, when and why; Approve, Request changes and Reject on your turn.
  bind         statekey (required)  State key holding the stages, in order: `{ id, title, rule, due, approvers: [{ id, name, avatar, decision, comment, at, for }], rounds }`; `rule` is `all` (default), `any` or a number, `decision` approved, changes or rejected, `due` a date it's due by, `for` the approver who handed it on, `rounds` earlier rounds' approvers (kept when it's sent again)
  me           any  The `id` of whoever's looking: on their turn, they get the buttons to decide
  owner        any  The `id` of whoever sent it: after changes or a rejection, they can send it again
  bindStatus   statekey  State key that gets `pending`, `changes`, `rejected` or `approved`, as it changes
  people       any  Who an approver can hand their turn to: `[{ id, name, avatar }]`
  readOnly     bool  Only shows where it stands: no buttons
  locale       string  How times are written (default: the document's `lang`)
  label        any  Names it for screen readers (default `Approval`)
  id           any  Element id (default: derived from the document)
  children: no
ui-whiteboard: A board without edges: draw with a pen, add sticky notes, shapes, arrows and text, select, move, resize and edit them, pan and zoom, undo, and export it as SVG.
  bind         statekey (required)  State key holding the items, in the board's units: `{ id, type, x, y, w, h, points, text, color }`; `type` is pen, note, rect, ellipse, arrow or text
  bindView     statekey  State key holding the view, `{ x, y, zoom }`, both ways
  tools        any  The tools offered, from select, hand, pen, note, rect, ellipse, arrow, text (default all)
  colors       any  The colours to pick from: CSS colours (default eight)
  readOnly     bool  Look and move around only
  height       any  Its height: px or a CSS length (default 480)
  label        any  Names it for screen readers (default `Whiteboard`)
  id           any  Element id (default: derived from the document)
  children: no
ui-mindmap: A mind map: a central topic with coloured branches on both sides; add, write, fold, move and delete topics from the keyboard or the mouse, pan, zoom, undo and export.
  bind         statekey (required)  State key holding the map: the central topic, `{ id, label, icon, note, children, collapsed, color }`, children the same; `icon` is a character or emoji before the label, `note` longer text for the topic (edited under the map)
  bindSelected statekey  State key that gets the `id` of the topic selected
  layout       one of: balanced, right  `balanced` (default: branches on both sides) or `right`
  colors       any  Colours for the first branches, in turn (default eight)
  readOnly     bool  Look, fold and move around only
  height       any  Its height: px or a CSS length (default 480)
  label        any  Names it for screen readers (default: the central topic)
  id           any  Element id (default: derived from the document)
  children: no
ui-timeline: Activity, newest first or as given: who did what and when, with field changes (old → new) and comments. Entries are `ui-timeline-item` children and/or `items`.
  items        any  Entries with the `ui-timeline-item` props, after any children. From state, like `{{ history }}`, it redraws as it changes
  label        any  Names it for screen readers (default `Activity`)
  group        one of: day  A heading over each day's entries: Today, Yesterday, a weekday, a date (entries' `when` a date and time, in order)
  relative     bool  Each `when` as how long ago (`5 min ago`, `3 h ago`), kept up to date, with the full date on hover
  since        any  Entries after this date and time (a last visit, say) are marked New; may use state
  limit        number  Show the first this many entries, then a button for the rest
  filters      bool  Menus over the feed to show one person's entries, or one `kind` of entry, from those it has
  bindFilter   statekey  With `filters`, a state key holding what's picked, `{ who, kind }` (null for all); setting it picks them
  hasMore      any  There are older entries on the server: once all here are shown, a Load more button fires `more` (the page adds them to `items`); may use state
  loading      any  While true, Load more says Loading… and waits; may use state
  children: yes
ui-timeline-item: One entry of a `ui-timeline`. Children go under its line.
  who          any  Who did it, shown first in bold
  action       any  What they did, after the name: `changed the status`, `commented`
  when         any  When: text (`4 Nov, 10:42`), or a date and time (`2026-11-04T10:42`) for the timeline's `group`, `relative` and `since`
  initials     any  In the avatar when there's no image (default: from `who`)
  avatar       any  Avatar image URL
  changes      any  Fields changed: `[{ field, from, to }]`, shown as from → to
  comment      any  Text they wrote, quoted under the line
  tone         one of: neutral, info, success, warning, danger, primary  The dot's colour, for an event rather than a person (with no `who`)
  kind         any  What sort of entry it is (`comment`, `status`, `file`), for the timeline's `filters`
  children: yes
ui-lightbox: Pictures that open over the page: step with the arrows or a swipe, zoom with the wheel, a pinch or a double click, and save.
  images       any (required)  `[{ src, thumb, alt, caption, download }]`, or addresses; may use state
  layout       one of: grid, row, masonry, stack  `grid` (default), `row` (scrolls sideways), `masonry`, or `stack`: the first large, the rest counted on it
  minWidth     number  The narrowest a thumbnail gets, in px (default 140)
  ratio        any  A thumbnail's shape, e.g. `1` or `"4 / 3"` (default 1; `masonry` keeps each picture's own)
  max          number  Thumbnails shown; the last says how many more there are
  captions     bool  Captions under the thumbnails too
  download     bool  A button saves the picture shown
  bind         statekey  State key for the open picture's place, from 0 (null: closed); set it to open one
  label        any  Names the pictures for screen readers (default `Images`)
  children: no
ui-query-builder: Conditions put together with and / or, nested in groups: for segments, alerts, rules, access. State gets the query, its words, and the rows that match.
  bind         statekey (required)  State key for the query: `{ op: and|or, not, rules: [{ field, operator, value } or another group] }`
  fields       any (required)  What rules are about: `[{ field, label, type, options, operators, unit }]`; `type`: text, number, currency, date, select, multiselect or boolean
  maxDepth     number  How deep groups nest (default 3; 1 for none)
  negate       bool  Groups can be negated (`not`)
  bindText     statekey  State key that gets the query in words
  bindValid    statekey  State key that gets true while every rule is filled in
  rows         any  Rows to try the query on; may use state
  bindMatches  statekey  With `rows`, state key that gets those that match
  showText     bool  The query in words under it
  label        any  Names it for screen readers (default `Conditions`)
  disabled     any  Shown, not changed
  locale       string  How numbers and dates are written (default: the document's `lang`, else the browser's)
  children: no
ui-transfer-list: Two lists: what there is and what's chosen, moved between with buttons, a double click, Enter or dragging.
  bind         statekey (required)  State key for the chosen values, a list in their order
  options      any (required)  All of them: values or `{ value, label, description, group, disabled }`; may use state
  titles       any  The two lists' names (default `[Available, Chosen]`)
  search       bool  A search box over each list (default true)
  reorderable  bool  The chosen ones can be put in order, by dragging or with Alt and the arrow keys
  max          number  The most that can be chosen
  height       any  Each list's height (default 260)
  disabled     any  Shown, not changed
  children: no
ui-tree-select: A choice from a hierarchy: a field that opens a searchable tree, for one node or several.
  bind         statekey (required)  State key for the chosen node's id, or with `multiple`, a list of ids
  nodes        any (required)  As `ui-tree`'s: `[{ id, label, children }]`; may use state
  multiple     bool  Check several; checking a node checks those under it
  leavesOnly   bool  Only nodes without children can be chosen (single choice)
  path         bool  Shows the chosen node with those above it
  search       bool  A search box over the tree (default true)
  expanded     any  As `ui-tree`'s
  clearable    bool  A button clears the choice (default true)
  placeholder  any  Default `Select…`
  label        any  Accessible name, when no visible label names it
  disabled     any  Boolean or expression
  invalid      any  Mark it wrong
  height       any  Most the tree grows to (default 280)
  parts: trigger
  children: no
ui-attachment: Files sent with a message or being sent: a name, size and picture, progress, what went wrong, and a button to remove each.
  files        any (required)  `[{ id, name, type, size, url, thumb, status, progress, error, text }]`; `status`: uploading, processing, done or error; may use state
  bindFiles    statekey  State key the files are in: they can be removed
  layout       one of: chips, cards  Default `chips`
  label        any  Names them for screen readers (default `Attachments`)
  children: no
ui-sources: What an answer is based on: numbered sources, and the `[1]`s in its text as links that show them.
  items        any (required)  `[{ title, url, text, site, date, page }]`, numbered in their order; may use state
  text         any  Text with `[1]`, `[2]` in it: each becomes a link that shows its source
  layout       one of: list, chips, fold  All of them (`list`), small (`chips`), or folded behind how many there are (`fold`, default)
  label        any  Default `Sources`
  children: no
ui-tool-call: Something an assistant or a job did, or asks leave to do: what, how it went, and what went in and out.
  title        any (required)  What was done, e.g. `Searched the orders`
  status       any  `pending`, `running`, `done`, `error` or `approval`; may use state
  name         any  The tool's own name, smaller
  input        any  What it was given; shown as JSON, or as it is when text
  output       any  What it answered
  error        any  What went wrong
  duration     any  Milliseconds it took
  open         bool  Starts open (with `approval` it always does)
  bindApproval statekey  With `status: approval`, state key that gets true or false; also `approve` and `deny` events
  label        any  Names it for screen readers
  children: no
ui-trace: The steps of a run, nested and against time: an assistant's, a job's, a request's. A step opens to what went in and out of it.
  spans        any (required)  The steps: `[{ id, parent, name, kind, start, duration, status, input, output, error, tokens, cost }]`, times in milliseconds from any start; may use state
  kinds        any  Colours by `kind`: `{ model: "#7c3aed" }`
  bindSpan     statekey  State key that gets the step clicked
  expanded     any  How deep it starts open (default every step)
  height       any  Most it grows to before it scrolls
  title        any  Shown over it
  label        any  Names it for screen readers (default `Trace`)
  children: no
ui-questionnaire: Questions answered one at a time or together: choices, text, numbers, a scale. For an assistant's questions, surveys and intake forms.
  questions    any (required)  `[{ id, question, description, type, options, other, required, min, max, labels }]`; `type`: choice (default), choices, text, number, scale, yesno; may use state
  bind         statekey (required)  State key for the answers, `{ id: answer }`
  mode         one of: steps, all  One question at a time (default), or all of them
  bindDone     statekey  State key that gets true once it's submitted; also a `submit` event with the answers
  skippable    bool  Questions that aren't required can be skipped (default true)
  submitLabel  any  Default `Send`
  doneText     any  Shown once it's submitted, over the answers
  title        any  Shown over it
  label        any  Names it for screen readers (default `Questions`)
  children: no
ui-tour: Steps that point at parts of the page one after another, for someone new to it. Draws nothing until it starts.
  bind         statekey (required)  State key for the step shown, from 0 (null: closed); set it to start
  steps        any (required)  `[{ target, title, text, side, image, set }]`: `target`, a CSS selector (none: in the middle); `side`: top, bottom, left or right; `set`: state to set first, e.g. `{ tab: billing }`
  autoStart    bool  Starts by itself, for someone who hasn't seen it (needs `id`)
  id           string  Remembered under this name in the browser once it's finished or skipped
  backdrop     bool  The rest of the page is dimmed (default true)
  interactive  bool  The part pointed at can be used while it's shown
  doneLabel    any  The last step's button (default `Done`)
  children: no
ui-banner: A message across the page: maintenance, an offer, a trial's end, a setting to finish. Children (links, buttons) go after it.
  text         any  The message
  title        any  In bold before it
  tone         one of: neutral, info, success, warning, danger, primary  Its colour (default `info`)
  variant      one of: soft, solid  Default `soft`
  icon         any  An icon name (with the icon kit) or a character
  bind         statekey  State key that's true while it's closed; with it, there's a close button
  remember     string  Once closed, stays closed in this browser, under this name (change it to show again)
  sticky       one of: top, bottom  Keeps to an edge of the window as the page scrolls
  align        one of: start, center  Default `center`
  until        any  Goes by itself at this time, e.g. `2026-12-01T06:00`

  url          any  Post the rows here in batches, `{ rows }` as JSON; answering `{ errors: [{ row, field, message }] }` (`row` counts from 0 in the batch) sends those back to be put right
  params       any  With `url`, more to send with each batch; may use state
  batchSize    number  With `url`, rows per request (default 200)
  accept       string  File types (default `.csv,.tsv,.txt,.xlsx`)

  skipInvalid  bool  Rows that aren't right can be left out (default true; false: all must be right)
  template     any  Offers an empty file to fill in: `true` (default), its name ending in `.csv` or `.xlsx`, or false

ui-form: A form whose fields are checked by `rules` as they're left and when it's submitted (`on: { submit: … }` runs only when all is right), which knows its unsaved changes. A `remote` rule asks the server (is this name taken?). Put a `ui-error-summary` and a `ui-save-bar` in it.
  rules        any  What each state key must be: `{ email: { label, required, type: email|url|number|date, min, max, minLength, maxLength, pattern, match: otherKey, message, remote } }`. Any of them may use state, e.g. `required: "{{ kind == 'company' }}"`. `remote: /api/available` (or `{ url, param, wait, message, headers }`) asks the server once the other rules pass, `wait` ms (default 400) after the value last changed: GET `url?value=…` (`param` renames it; `{value}` in the url is replaced instead), answered by `true`, `{ valid: true }`, or what's wrong (`false`, a text, `{ valid: false, message }`). A submit waits for it; if the server can't be reached the value passes (it's checked again when sent) and the form fires `failed`
  bindErrors   statekey  State key that gets `{ key: message }` for the fields left so far (all of them once submitting was tried); give it to each `ui-field`'s `error`
  bindValid    statekey  State key that gets true while every rule is met (not while a `remote` one is being asked)

  bindTried    statekey  State key that gets true once submitting was tried with something wrong
  keys         any  State keys whose changes are unsaved changes (default: those with `rules`)
  bindDirty    statekey  State key that gets true while there are unsaved changes; set it to false once saved (a `submit` that succeeds does)
  guard        bool  Asks before leaving the page with unsaved changes
  guardText    any  What's asked (default `You have unsaved changes that will be lost.`)
  disabled     any  Nothing can be changed or submitted, e.g. `{{ saving }}`
  columns      number  Lays what's in it out in columns, 1–6; two and then one as it narrows. Children take more with `span` (`ui-field`, `ui-form-section`) or `style: { grid-column: 1 / -1 }`
  children: yes
ui-error-summary: What's wrong in the `ui-form` it's in, listed once submitting was tried; each message goes to its field.
  title        any  Default `There's a problem` / `There are {n} problems`

ui-save-bar: Shown while the `ui-form` it's in has unsaved changes: Save submits the form, Discard puts its fields back. Children go before the buttons.

  saveLabel    any  The button that submits the form (default `Save`)
  discardLabel any  The button that puts the fields back as they were (default `Discard`); false for none

  layout       one of: stacked, aside  The heading above the fields (default), or `aside`: beside them (up to 240px wide) while there's room

  fields       any (required)  The fields of a row: `[{ field, label, type, options, placeholder, width, required, min, max, pattern, unique, message, default, compute, format, currency, decimals, summary }]`. `type`: text, multiline, number, currency, date, time, email, tel, url, select, combobox (typed, picked from `options` as you type), checkbox, or computed (`compute: qty * price`, over the row's fields and state)

ui-event-calendar: Events in a month grid, a week of hours, or a list by day, coloured by category, with a toolbar to move through time. Clicks go to `bindEvent` (an event) and `bindDay` (a day, e.g. to add one).
```
