```
ui-toggle-group: A row of toggles where one at most is pressed; pressing it again clears it. With `multiple`, any number can be pressed.
  bind         statekey (required)  State key holding the pressed value, or null (a list of them with `multiple`)
  options      any (required)  Array of values or `{ value, label, disabled }`; may use state
  multiple     bool  Let several be pressed; `bind` holds a list
  variant      one of: default, outline  Default `default`
  size         one of: default, sm, lg  Default `default`
  disabled     any  Disable every option
  children: no
ui-theme-toggle: Switches the page between the system's colour scheme, light and dark, and remembers the choice in the browser.
  labels       any  Button text as `{ system, light, dark }`; default System, Light, Dark
  variant      one of: default, outline  Default `outline`
  size         one of: default, sm, lg  Default `sm`
  children: no
ui-theme-option: Picks one choice of a theme option (`theme.options`), such as a palette or a corner radius, for every page, and remembers it in the browser.
  option       string (required)  The theme option it picks, from `theme.options`, e.g. `palette`
  bind         statekey  State key that gets the choice, e.g. `rose`, to show it or use it on the page; setting it picks that choice
  swatch       any  A token each choice is shown with as a colour dot, e.g. `color.primary`, or a list of them
  label        any  The group's name for screen readers (default: the option's label)
  variant      one of: default, outline  Default `outline`
  size         one of: default, sm, lg  Default `sm`
  children: no
ui-theme-panel: A labelled `ui-theme-option` for each theme option (the kits' and the document's), and the mode. Put it in a `ui-popover` for a Theme button.
  options      any  The options to show, in order, e.g. `[palette, radius]` (default: every theme option, the palette first and chart colours last)
  mode         bool  Show the light / dark mode too (default true)
  children: no
ui-theme-colors: Colour inputs, typed as hex or picked: a primary and a second brand colour, each with an optional gradient end, and the backgrounds of the page, cards, popovers, dialogs, sheets and the sidebar for the mode showing. Changing one picks the option's `custom` choice; the colours are remembered with the other theme choices.
  option       string  The option whose `custom` choice the colours make (default `palette`)
  gradients    bool  Gradient ends for the primary and second colour (default true)
  backgrounds  bool  Background colours for the page, cards, popovers, dialogs, sheets and the sidebar, per mode (default true)
  children: no
ui-dialog: A modal window. Escape, the ✕ or a click outside closes it.
  trigger      any  Text of a button that opens it (or open it from your own button, see README)
  triggerVariant one of: default, secondary, destructive, outline, ghost, link, brand  The trigger button's variant (default `outline`)
  title        any  Heading
  description  any  Text under the heading
  id           any  Element id (default: derived from the document)
  parts: trigger, header, title, description
  children: yes
ui-alert-dialog: A modal that needs an answer: only its own buttons close it.
  trigger      any  Text of a button that opens it (or open it from your own button, see README)
  triggerVariant one of: default, secondary, destructive, outline, ghost, link, brand  The trigger button's variant (default `outline`)
  title        any  Heading
  description  any  Text under the heading
  id           any  Element id (default: derived from the document)
  parts: trigger, header, title, description
  children: yes
ui-sheet: A modal panel along one edge of the screen.
  trigger      any  Text of a button that opens it
  triggerVariant one of: default, secondary, destructive, outline, ghost, link, brand  The trigger button's variant (default `outline`)
  title        any  Heading
  description  any  Text under the heading
  side         one of: right, left, top, bottom  Edge it slides from (default `right`)
  id           any  Element id (default: derived from the document)
  parts: trigger, header, title, description
  children: yes
ui-drawer: A panel that slides up from the bottom, and that a drag down (or Escape, or the ✕) closes.
  trigger      any  Text of a button that opens it
  triggerVariant one of: default, secondary, destructive, outline, ghost, link, brand  The trigger button's variant (default `outline`)
  title        any  Heading
  description  any  Text under the heading
  width        any  Its widest, centred on a wide screen (default: the whole width)
  id           any  Element id (default: derived from the document)
  parts: trigger, header, title, description
  children: yes
ui-dialog-close: A button that closes the dialog, alert dialog or sheet it is in. Its own `on.click` actions run too.
  label        any (required)  Button text
  variant      one of: default, secondary, destructive, outline, ghost, link, brand  Default `default`
  children: yes
ui-dialog-footer: A row of buttons at the bottom of a dialog.
  children: yes
ui-popover: A button that opens floating content next to it. A click outside or Escape closes it.
  trigger      any (required)  Text of the button that opens it
  triggerVariant one of: default, secondary, destructive, outline, ghost, link, brand  The trigger button's variant (default `outline`)
  triggerSize  one of: default, sm, lg, icon  The trigger button's size (default `default`)
  side         one of: bottom, top, right, left  Where it opens, next to the trigger (default `bottom`)
  align        one of: center, start, end  Alignment along that side (default `center`; menus `start`)
  id           any  Element id (default: derived from the document)
  parts: trigger
  children: yes
ui-dropdown-menu: A button that opens a list of actions. Children are `ui-menu-item`, `ui-menu-label` and `ui-menu-separator`.
  trigger      any (required)  Text of the button that opens it
  triggerVariant one of: default, secondary, destructive, outline, ghost, link, brand  The trigger button's variant (default `outline`)
  triggerSize  one of: default, sm, lg, icon  The trigger button's size (default `default`)
  side         one of: bottom, top, right, left  Where it opens, next to the trigger (default `bottom`)
  align        one of: center, start, end  Alignment along that side (default `center`; menus `start`)
  id           any  Element id (default: derived from the document)
  parts: trigger
  children: yes
ui-split-button: A primary action with an arrow that opens a menu of secondary ones. Its `on.click` is the primary action; children are the menu's `ui-menu-item`, `ui-menu-label` and `ui-menu-separator`.
  label        any (required)  The primary action's text
  variant      one of: default, secondary, destructive, outline, ghost, link, brand  Both buttons' variant (default `default`)
  size         one of: default, sm, lg, icon  Both buttons' size (default `default`; not `icon`)
  disabled     any  Disable the primary action (the menu still opens)
  menuLabel    any  The arrow's name for screen readers (default `More actions`)
  side         one of: bottom, top, right, left  Where the menu opens (default `bottom`)
  align        one of: center, start, end  The menu's alignment (default `end`: its right edge under the arrow)
  id           any  The menu's element id (default: derived from the document)
  parts: primary, trigger
  children: yes
ui-context-menu: A menu opened with a right-click (or Shift+F10, or the menu key) on its area, at the pointer. `ui-menu-item`, `ui-menu-label` and `ui-menu-separator` children are the menu; any other children are the area.
  bind         statekey  State key that gets what was right-clicked: the nearest `data-context` value (JSON or text), or a data table's row
  label        any  The menu's accessible name (default `Actions`)
  disabled     any  Leave the browser's own menu in place, e.g. `{{ !editing }}`
  id           any  The menu's element id (default: derived from the document)
  parts: menu
  children: yes
ui-menu-sub: An item that opens a submenu beside it, on hover, Enter, Space or Right; Left or Escape closes it. Children are menu items, as in any menu.
  label        any (required)  The item that opens the submenu
  disabled     any  Boolean or expression
  id           any  The submenu's element id (default: derived from the document)
  parts: trigger, menu
  children: yes
ui-menu-checkbox: A menu item that turns a setting on and off (`role=menuitemcheckbox`), with a check while it's on. Choosing it flips `bind` and closes the menu (unless `keepOpen`).
  label        any (required)  Item text
  bind         statekey (required)  State key holding `true` / `false`; choosing the item flips it
  shortcut     any  Keyboard hint shown on the right
  disabled     any  Boolean or expression
  keepOpen     bool  The menu stays open when it's chosen, for flipping several settings in a row
  parts: shortcut
  children: no
ui-menu-radio-group: Menu items that pick one of several values (`role=menuitemradio`), with a dot by the chosen one. Choosing one writes its value to `bind` and closes the menu (unless `keepOpen`).
  bind         statekey (required)  State key holding the chosen value
  options      any (required)  Values, or `{ value, label, shortcut, disabled }`
  label        any  Accessible name of the group
  keepOpen     bool  The menu stays open when one is chosen
  children: no
ui-menubar: A bar of menus, as at the top of an application: `ui-menubar-menu` children. Left and Right move along the bar (an open menu follows), Down opens a menu, and hovering moves between open menus.
  label        any  Accessible name (default `Menu bar`)
  children: yes
ui-menubar-menu: One menu of a `ui-menubar`: its name in the bar, and menu items as children (`ui-menu-item`, `-checkbox`, `-radio-group`, `-sub`, `-label`, `-separator`).
  label        any (required)  The menu's name in the bar, e.g. `File`
  disabled     any  Boolean or expression
  id           any  The menu's element id (default: derived from the document)
  children: yes
ui-navigation-menu: A site's navigation: `ui-navigation-link` children are links, and `ui-navigation-item` children open a panel of links (or anything) on hover or click. Down opens a panel and moves into it; Escape closes it.
  label        any  Accessible name of the navigation (default `Main`)
  align        one of: start, center, end  Where panels line up with their item (default `start`)
  children: yes
ui-navigation-item: An item of a `ui-navigation-menu` that opens a panel: its children, usually `ui-navigation-link`s with descriptions, laid out as you like.
  label        any (required)  The item's text in the bar
  width        any  The panel's width (default: its content's, at most the window's)
  id           any  The panel's element id (default: derived from the document)
  children: yes
ui-navigation-link: A link in a `ui-navigation-menu`: in the bar, or in an item's panel, where it shows its `description` under the text.
  label        any (required)  Link text
  href         any (required)  Where it goes
  description  any  A line under the text, in a panel
  active       any  The current page (`aria-current=page`)
  children: no
ui-menu-item: An action in a `ui-dropdown-menu`. Choosing it runs its `on.click` and closes the menu.
  label        any (required)  Item text
  shortcut     any  Keyboard hint shown on the right, e.g. `⌘S`
  variant      one of: default, destructive  Default `default`
  href         any  Make it a link
  disabled     any  Boolean or expression
  parts: shortcut
  children: no
ui-menu-separator: A line between groups of menu items.
  children: no
ui-menu-label: A heading inside a menu.
  text         any (required)  Heading for the items below
  children: no
ui-tooltip: A short tip shown when its children are hovered or focused. It describes the first child for screen readers.
  text         any (required)  The tip
  side         one of: top, bottom, left, right  Default `top`
  id           any  The tip's element id (default: derived from the document)
  parts: tip
  children: yes
ui-hover-card: A preview card shown when its trigger is hovered or focused. Children are the card.
  trigger      any (required)  Text that shows the card when hovered or focused
  href         any  Make the trigger a link
  parts: trigger, card
  children: yes
ui-toaster: Shows toasts in a corner of the screen. Set `bind` to a toast to add it to the stack; each one hides after its `duration`, and the key is cleared for the next.
  bind         statekey (required)  State key to set to a toast, `{ title, description, variant, duration }`, to show it
  duration     number  Milliseconds before a toast hides (default 4000); 0 keeps it until dismissed
  max          number  Toasts shown at once (default 3); the oldest goes first
  parts: toast
  children: no
ui-sidebar-layout: A page with a sidebar. Children: a `ui-sidebar`, then the main area's content. With `bind`, a `ui-sidebar-trigger` opens and closes it.
  bind         statekey  State key holding whether the sidebar is open (`true` / `false`)
  collapsible  one of: offcanvas, icon, none  How it closes: `offcanvas` (slides away, default), `icon` (narrows to icons) or `none`
  variant      one of: sidebar, inset, floating  `sidebar` (default), `inset` (the main area is a raised panel) or `floating`
  side         one of: left, right  Default `left`
  width        any  The open sidebar's width (default 16rem)
  remember     any  Keep open or closed across reloads, in the browser's storage: `true` (under `bind`'s name) or a name shared by the pages that should agree
  parts: main
  children: yes
ui-sidebar: The sidebar's panel, inside a `ui-sidebar-layout`. Children: `ui-sidebar-header`, `ui-sidebar-content` and `ui-sidebar-footer`.
  label        any  Names the navigation for screen readers (default `Sidebar`)
  parts: inner
  children: yes
ui-sidebar-header: The top of a `ui-sidebar`, e.g. a logo or a team switcher.
  children: yes
ui-sidebar-content: The scrolling middle of a `ui-sidebar`. Children: `ui-sidebar-group`s.
  children: yes
ui-sidebar-footer: The bottom of a `ui-sidebar`, e.g. the signed-in user.
  children: yes
ui-sidebar-group: A labelled list in a sidebar. Children: `ui-sidebar-item`s, and `ui-sidebar-action`s for buttons beside the label.
  label        any  The group's heading, e.g. `Platform`
  parts: label, list
  children: yes
ui-sidebar-item: An entry in a sidebar group: a link, or a button that runs its `on.click`. Children are a sub-menu of more `ui-sidebar-item`s, opened and closed by the item, and `ui-sidebar-action`s for buttons at the end of its row.
  label        any (required)  The item's text
  icon         any  An icon name (with the icon kit) or a character, shown before the label
  href         any  Make it a link
  active       any  Marks the current page (boolean or expression)
  badge        any  A count or short text on the right
  open         bool  With children: start with its sub-menu open
  parts: label, list
  children: yes
ui-sidebar-action: A small button beside a `ui-sidebar-group`'s label or at the end of a `ui-sidebar-item`'s row, e.g. Add project or More. It runs its `on.click`; with `ui-menu-item`, `ui-menu-label` and `ui-menu-separator` children it opens them as a dropdown menu instead.
  label        any (required)  What it does, for screen readers and as its tooltip, e.g. `Add project`
  icon         any  An icon name (with the icon kit) or a character (default: three dots)
  showOnHover  bool  On an item: hidden until the row is hovered or has focus
  parts: menu
  children: yes
ui-sidebar-trigger: A button that opens and closes the sidebar of the `ui-sidebar-layout` it is in (one with `bind`).
  label        any  Its name for screen readers (default `Toggle sidebar`)
  children: yes
ui-combobox: A searchable select: one or many values, groups, async options, creatable values, full keyboard support.
  bind         statekey  State key holding the value (an array with `multiple`)
  options      any  Values, `{ value, label, description, disabled }`, or groups `{ label, options }`. From data, or a state path
  valueField   string  Field of an option object holding its value (default `value`)
  labelField   string  Field holding its label (default `label`)
  descriptionField string  Field holding its description (default `description`)
  imageField   string  Field holding a picture shown before its label: an avatar, a flag, a logo (default `image`)
  badgeField   string  Field holding short text shown after its label: a count, a status (default `badge`)
  multiple     bool  Choose several values, shown as removable chips
  searchable   bool  Type to filter (default true)
  clearable    bool  Show a button that clears the value
  creatable    bool  Offer to create a value from what was typed
  searchUrl    any  Load options as you type: GET `<url>?q=<text>`, answering an array
  labels       any  Options for values chosen before they're searched for, so they show their names: `[{ value, label }]`; may use state
  lookup       bool  With `searchUrl`: names of chosen values it doesn't know are asked for, GET `<url>?values=a,b`
  minChars     number  Characters typed before searching `searchUrl` (default 1)
  debounce     number  Milliseconds to wait after typing before searching (default 250)
  closeOnSelect bool  Close the menu after choosing (default: unless `multiple`)
  hideSelected bool  Leave chosen options out of the menu (default: with `multiple`)
  fixed        any  Values that can't be removed
  value        any  Initial value, when not bound
  placeholder  any  Shown while nothing is chosen (default `Select…`)
  label        any  Accessible name, when no visible label points at `parts.input`
  name         string  Form field name: hidden inputs carry the value(s)
  disabled     any  Boolean or expression
  loading      any  Show the loading indicator, e.g. `{{ fetching }}`
  noOptionsText any  Default `No options`
  loadingText  any  Default `Loading…`
  createText   any  Default `Create "{input}"`
  id           any  Element id (default: derived from the document)
  parts: control, input, menu
  children: no
ui-command: A search box over a list of actions, filtered as you type; Up and Down move, Enter runs the active one. Children are `ui-command-group`, `ui-command-item` and `ui-command-separator`.
  placeholder  any  The search box's placeholder (default `Type a command or search…`)
  label        any  The search box's accessible name (default: the placeholder)
  empty        any  Shown when nothing matches (default `No results found.`)
  id           any  Element id (default: derived from the document)
  rank         bool  Put the best matches first, in each group and of the groups (default true); false keeps the items' order
  bindSearch   statekey  State key that holds the search text, both ways: to fetch items for it, say
  loading      any  True while items are being fetched, e.g. `{{ searching }}`: a Loading row shows, and the empty message waits
  loadingText  any  The Loading row's text (default `Loading…`)
  parts: search, input, list, loading, empty
  children: yes
ui-command-dialog: A `ui-command` in a modal, opened by its trigger, a `shortcut`, or a button with `commandfor` its id. Running an item closes it.
  placeholder  any  The search box's placeholder (default `Type a command or search…`)
  label        any  The search box's accessible name (default: the placeholder)
  empty        any  Shown when nothing matches (default `No results found.`)
  id           any  Element id (default: derived from the document)
  rank         bool  Put the best matches first, in each group and of the groups (default true); false keeps the items' order
  bindSearch   statekey  State key that holds the search text, both ways: to fetch items for it, say
  loading      any  True while items are being fetched, e.g. `{{ searching }}`: a Loading row shows, and the empty message waits
  loadingText  any  The Loading row's text (default `Loading…`)
  trigger      any  Text of a button that opens it
  triggerVariant one of: default, secondary, destructive, outline, ghost, link, brand  The trigger button's variant (default `outline`)
  shortcut     string  Keys that open and close it from anywhere on the page, e.g. `mod+k` (⌘K on Apple devices, Ctrl+K elsewhere)
  title        any  Its accessible name (default `Command palette`)
  parts: trigger, search, input, list, loading, empty
  children: yes
ui-command-group: Items under a heading in a command palette. It hides while none of its items match.
  heading      any  Its heading
  id           any  Element id (default: derived from the document)
  parts: heading
  children: yes
ui-command-item: An action in a command palette: clicking it, or Enter while it is active, runs its `on.click`.
  label        any (required)  Item text, matched as you type
  keywords     any  More words that find it: a string or a list
  icon         any  An icon name when the icon kit is registered (`settings`), or text such as an emoji
  shortcut     any  Keyboard hint shown on the right, e.g. `⌘P`
  href         any  Make it a link
  disabled     any  Boolean or expression
  page         string  Opens the `ui-command-page` with this `id`, and the palette stays open (Backspace in the empty search box goes back)
  parts: shortcut
  children: no
ui-command-page: A page of a command palette: items (and groups) shown in place of the rest when an item with its `page` is chosen. Backspace in the empty search box goes back.
  id           string (required)  What an item's `page` opens it by
  title        any  Shown in the search box while it's open (default: the id)
  children: yes
ui-command-separator: A line between groups in a command palette, hidden while searching.
  children: no
ui-conversation: A scrolling chat log that keeps to its latest message as messages arrive, unless you've scrolled up to read; then a button jumps back down. Children are `ui-message`s, followed by `messages`. Its `parts.bubble`, `parts.avatar` and so on style the messages drawn from `messages`.
  messages     any  Array of messages, after any children. From state, like `{{ messages }}`, it redraws as it changes
  typing       any  Show a typing indicator after the last message, e.g. `{{ waiting }}`
  render       any  How messages' `ui` without `html` is rendered: `{ browser, url }`, as on `ui-message`
  markdown     bool  Show messages as Markdown, as on `ui-message` (default: when irender-markdown-kit is registered)
  assistant    any  The typing indicator's sender: `{ name, avatar, initials }`
  empty        any  Text shown while `messages` is empty
  label        any  Names the conversation for screen readers (default `Conversation`)
  height       any  Number (px) or CSS length
  maxHeight    any  Number (px) or CSS length: grows with the messages up to this
  actions      any  Buttons under each message: `[copy, retry, edit, up, down]`; see `ui-message`
  parts: log, empty, latest, avatar, body, meta, bubble, ui, thread, replies
  children: yes
ui-message: One chat message: a bubble with the sender's avatar, name and time, and an optional thread of replies. Children go in the bubble after the text.
  role         one of: assistant, user, system  Who it's from: `assistant` (default, on the left), `user` (on the right) or `system` (centred)
  content      any  The text, as Markdown with `markdown` (headings, lists, code, tables, links); otherwise plain, line breaks kept
  markdown     bool  Show `content` as Markdown (default: when irender-markdown-kit is registered)
  streaming    any  The content is still arriving: Markdown formatting left open at its end shows as it will once closed
  name         any  Sender's name, shown above the bubble
  time         any  When it was sent, as text, shown after the name
  avatar       any  Avatar image URL
  initials     any  Shown in the avatar when there's no image
  html         any  UI after the text, rendered on a server: by `render_ui` (the CLI renders each message's `ui` into it), or `irender render --embed`. Shown only in trusted documents
  ui           any  UI after the text as an iRender document or node, for `render` to render when there's no `html`
  render       any  How a `ui` without `html` is rendered: `{ browser, url }`. `browser` is irender-wasm's `.wasm` file, to render it in the page; `url` is your server's render endpoint, which gets `{ ui }` and answers with the markup, used when there's no `browser` or it can't render it
  messageId    any  Its id, for `actions`
  actions      any  Buttons under it: `[copy, retry, edit, up, down]`. A `ui-chat-input` on the page does the rest: `retry` asks again, `edit` puts a message of yours back in the box, `up` and `down` write the message's `feedback`. Each fires `messageaction`
  feedback     any  `up` or `down`: which of the two is pressed
  sources      any  What it's based on, under it: as `ui-sources`' `items`
  attachments  any  Files sent with it, over it: as `ui-attachment`'s `files`
  replies      any  A thread: an array of messages shown under it, folded away behind `N replies`. May use state
  open         bool  Show the thread unfolded
  parts: avatar, body, meta, bubble, ui, thread, replies
  children: yes
ui-typing-indicator: Three bouncing dots that say a reply is on its way. Takes the text colour.
  label        any  What's happening, for screen readers; default `Typing`
  children: no
ui-chat-input: The box a chat message is written in. Enter sends and Shift+Enter starts a new line. Sending appends `{ id, role: user, content }` to `messages`, runs the document's `on.send` actions, and with `endpoint` asks it for the reply, streaming it into a new assistant message; while it streams, the send button stops it. With `threads` and `thread` it keeps a list of conversations. Children go in the toolbar, left of the send button.
  messages     statekey (required)  State key of the messages array: sending appends the user's message, and the reply
  endpoint     any  URL to POST `{ messages }` to. The reply may be JSON (a message, or `{ content }`), plain text, or server-sent events, which stream into the reply as they arrive
  body         any  More to send with each request, beside `messages`, e.g. `{ model: "{{ model }}" }`; may use state
  headers      any  Request headers, e.g. `{ authorization: "Bearer {{ token }}" }`; may use state
  bindFiles    statekey  State key of files to send with the next message (a `ui-file-upload`'s, or a `ui-attachment`'s): they become its `attachments`, and the key is emptied
  bind         statekey  State key holding the text being written
  waiting      statekey  State key set true from sending until the reply starts: give it to the conversation's `typing`
  threads      statekey  State key of an array of threads, `{ id, title, messages }`: the messages live in them, and `messages` shows the current one's. Needs `thread`
  thread       statekey  State key of the current thread's id; null for a new one, started by the first message
  placeholder  any  Default `Send a message…`
  label        any  Names the text box for screen readers (default `Message`)
  suggestions  any  Prompts shown while the conversation is empty; clicking one sends it
  disabled     any  Boolean or expression
  parts: suggestions, box, input, toolbar, send
  children: yes
ui-carousel: Slides in a row that scrolls sideways and snaps to each one: images, cards, anything. Its buttons, Left and Right on the focused track, and swiping move a slide at a time. Children are the slides.
  label        any  Names the carousel for screen readers (default `Carousel`)
  size         any  Each slide's width: number (px) or CSS length; default `min(280px, 85%)`
  gap          any  Space between slides: number (px) or CSS length; default 12
  dots         bool  A dot per slide under it, the current one marked; each goes to its slide
  loop         bool  Next at the end goes to the first slide, previous at the start to the last
  autoplay     number  Move on every this many ms, round and round, with a pause button; it waits while hovered or focused
  parts: track, previous, next, dots, play
  children: yes
ui-calendar: An inline calendar: days (with a time), months, quarters or years; one, a range or several; limits, presets, financial years and full keyboard support.
  bind         statekey  State key holding the value: `2026-03-01` (with `time`, `2026-03-01T14:30`; `2026-W09` (an ISO week), `2026-03`, `2026-Q1` or `2026` for the other pickers), `{ from, to }` with `mode: range` (with `time`, `{ from: 2026-03-02T09:00, to: 2026-03-06T17:00 }`), a list with `multiple`
  value        any  Starting value, when not bound
  picker       one of: day, week, month, quarter, year  What is picked: `day` (default), `week` (a whole week, Monday to Sunday, from the days), `month`, `quarter` or `year`
  mode         one of: single, range, multiple  `single` (default), `range` or `multiple`
  time         bool  A time as well as the day: one, or with `mode: range` a start and an end time (days only, not `multiple`)
  step         number  With `time`, minutes between times (default 1)
  min          any  Earliest date: `2026-01-01`, or `today`, `today-30d`, `today+1y`; may use state
  max          any  Latest date, as `min`
  disabledDates any  Dates that can't be picked: `2026-12-25`, or `{ from, to }`; may use state
  disabledDays any  Weekdays that can't be picked: 0 Sunday … 6 Saturday, e.g. `[0, 6]`
  months       number  Months shown side by side (default 1; 2 suits ranges)
  weekStart    number  First day of the week, 0 Sunday … 6 Saturday (default: the locale's)
  fiscalStart  number  Month a financial year starts, 1–12 (default 1); quarters and years follow it
  presets      any  Shortcuts beside the calendar: names (`last7`, `thisMonth`, `lastQuarter`, `yearToDate`, …) or `{ label, from, to }`
  dropdowns    bool  Month and year menus in place of the caption, for dates far away such as birthdays
  bindRange    statekey  State key that gets the dates the value covers, `{ from, to }`: a chart's or a table's filter
  compare      any  With `mode: range`, a period to compare with: `true`, or the kinds offered, from `previous`, `lastYear` and `custom`
  bindCompare  statekey  With `compare`, a state key holding the comparison, `{ type, from, to }` (the dates it covers), or null while it's off
  name         string  Form field name: hidden inputs carry the value (`name[from]` and `name[to]` for a range)
  locale       string  Locale for names and formats (default: the document's `lang`, else the browser's)
  label        any  Accessible name
  id           any  Element id (default: derived from the document)
  clearable    bool  A Clear button under the calendar
  children: no

  bind         statekey  State key holding the value: `2026-03-01` (with `time`, `2026-03-01T14:30`; `2026-W09` (an ISO week), `2026-03`, `2026-Q1` or `2026` for the other pickers), `{ from, to }` with `mode: range` (with `time`, `{ from: 2026-03-02T09:00, to: 2026-03-06T17:00 }`), a list with `multiple`
  value        any  Starting value, when not bound
  picker       one of: day, week, month, quarter, year  What is picked: `day` (default), `week` (a whole week, Monday to Sunday, from the days), `month`, `quarter` or `year`
  mode         one of: single, range, multiple  `single` (default), `range` or `multiple`
  time         bool  A time as well as the day: one, or with `mode: range` a start and an end time (days only, not `multiple`)
  step         number  With `time`, minutes between times (default 1)
  min          any  Earliest date: `2026-01-01`, or `today`, `today-30d`, `today+1y`; may use state

  disabledDates any  Dates that can't be picked: `2026-12-25`, or `{ from, to }`; may use state

  months       number  Months shown side by side (default 1; 2 suits ranges)
  weekStart    number  First day of the week, 0 Sunday … 6 Saturday (default: the locale's)
  fiscalStart  number  Month a financial year starts, 1–12 (default 1); quarters and years follow it
  presets      any  Shortcuts beside the calendar: names (`last7`, `thisMonth`, `lastQuarter`, `yearToDate`, …) or `{ label, from, to }`
  dropdowns    bool  Month and year menus in place of the caption, for dates far away such as birthdays
  bindRange    statekey  State key that gets the dates the value covers, `{ from, to }`: a chart's or a table's filter
  compare      any  With `mode: range`, a period to compare with: `true`, or the kinds offered, from `previous`, `lastYear` and `custom`
  bindCompare  statekey  With `compare`, a state key holding the comparison, `{ type, from, to }` (the dates it covers), or null while it's off

  locale       string  Locale for names and formats (default: the document's `lang`, else the browser's)

  input        bool  A text field to type the value in (`15/03/2026`, `Mar 15`, `today`), with a button beside it for the calendar

  placeholder  any  Shown while nothing is picked (default `Pick a date`, `Pick a range`, …)
  clearable    bool  A button in the field that clears the value

ui-color-picker: A colour: picked on an area with hue and opacity sliders, typed as any CSS colour, taken from the screen, or chosen from swatches. A button opens it in a popover; `inline` shows it on the page.
  bind         statekey  State key holding the colour as text in `format` (`#1e3a8a`), or null
  value        any  Starting colour, when not bound
  format       one of: hex, rgb, hsl  How the colour is written: `hex` (default, `#1e3a8a`, `#1e3a8a80` with opacity), `rgb` (`rgb(30, 58, 138)`) or `hsl` (`hsl(224, 64%, 33%)`)
  alpha        bool  An opacity slider too
  swatches     any  Colours to pick with one click: CSS colours, or `{ value, label }`
  custom       bool  The area, sliders and text field (default true); false leaves just the swatches
  eyedropper   bool  A button to take a colour from the screen, where the browser has one (default true)
  inline       bool  The panel on the page, without the button and popover
  placeholder  any  The button's text while there's no colour (default `Pick a colour`)
  clearable    bool  A button that clears the colour (to null)
  align        one of: start, end  The popover's edge lined up with the button (default `start`)
  name         string  Form field name: a hidden input carries the colour
  label        any  Accessible name
  disabled     any  Boolean or expression
  id           any  Element id (default: derived from the document)
  parts: trigger, input, popover
  children: no
ui-data-table: A data table: sorting, column filters, search, paging, row selection with bulk actions, expandable rows, a View menu and summaries. Children are `ui-data-table-column`s (a cell template, with the row as `row`), `ui-data-table-toolbar`, `ui-data-table-bulk` and `ui-data-table-detail`.
  rows         any  The rows: an array of objects, from data or state (or use `url`)
  url          any  Load rows from an API in batches: GET `<url>?offset=&limit=&sort=&q=&filters=`, answering `{ rows, total }` or an array. A query's first batch also asks `facets=` (select filters' fields) and `summary=` (`field:sum`, …); answering `facets: { field: [{ value, count }] }` and `summary: { "field:sum": n }` makes the filters and footer cover every matching row
  params       any  Extra query parameters for `url`; may use state, and a change reloads
  expand       any  Joins records from a `ui-data-source` into the rows drawn: `{ owner: { source: people, from: ownerId } }` puts the record whose id is in `ownerId` in `owner`, for columns like `owner.name`. Only the rows on the page are asked for, together; their cells pulse until it arrives
  columns      any  Columns as objects with the `ui-data-table-column` props, for tables with no cell templates
  rowKey       string  Field that identifies a row, for selection (default `id`; else its position)
  selectable   bool  A checkbox per row and a select-all box in the header
  search       any  A search box above the table: `true`, or its placeholder text
  searchFields any  Fields the search looks in (default: every column's field)
  sort         any  Starting sort: `field`, `-field` for descending, or a list of them
  filter       any  Filters from outside the table, e.g. a chart's `bind`: `{ field: condition }`, as `ui-chart`'s `filter`
  paging       one of: pages, more, scroll, none  `pages` (default): a pager; `more`: a Load more button; `scroll`: the next batch as you reach the bottom; `none`
  pageSize     number  Rows per page, or per batch with `more` and `scroll` (default 10; 0 shows every row)
  childrenField string  Rows nest: the field holding a row's child rows (default `children`); `true` there means load them from `childrenUrl`
  parentField  string  Rows nest: flat rows name their parent's key in this field, e.g. `parentId`
  childrenUrl  any  Load a row's children when it's first opened: GET `<url>?parent=<key>`, answering an array or `{ rows }`
  expanded     bool  Nested rows start open (default false)
  selectChildren bool  Nested rows: picking a row picks the rows under it, and a row is picked when all under it are (default true)
  virtual      bool  Keep only the rows in view in the page, for long tables; scrolls inside `height` (default 480)
  rowHeight    number  With `virtual`, a row's height to start from before rows are measured (default 41)
  pageSizes    any  Choices for rows per page (default `[10, 20, 50, 100]`; `[]` hides it)
  columnsMenu  bool  A View menu that shows and hides columns (default true)
  groupBy      any  Groups the rows by this field, each group under a header row with its count and subtotals (may use state)
  bindGroupBy  statekey  State key holding the field the rows are grouped by (or null), set from the View menu
  resizable    bool  Columns can be made wider or narrower by dragging their header's edge
  reorderable  bool  Columns can be moved by dragging their header, or Alt and the arrow keys on it
  bindColumns  statekey  State key holding the columns' layout, `{ order, widths, hidden }`, to keep it
  export       any  An Export button that downloads the rows that pass the filters as CSV, or as Excel with a name ending in `.xlsx`: `true`, or the file's name
  title        any  Accessible name of the table
  emptyText    any  Shown when no row matches (default `No results.`)
  locale       string  Locale for formatted numbers and dates (default: the document's `lang`, else the browser's)
  height       any  Most the table grows to before it scrolls, with the header kept in view
  striped      bool  Shade every other row
  loading      any  Dim the rows and mark the table busy, e.g. `{{ fetching }}`
  bindSelection statekey  State key holding the selected rows' keys (a list)
  bindSort     statekey  State key holding the sort: `field`, `-field`, a list of them, or null
  bindFilters  statekey  State key holding the column filters, `{ field: condition }`: give it to a chart's `filter` to filter both
  bindSearch   statekey  State key holding the search text
  bindPage     statekey  State key holding the page number, from 1
  bindView     statekey  State key that gets the rows that pass the filters and search, sorted, every page: a chart's `data`
  bindRow      statekey  State key that gets the row last clicked (or opened with Enter)
  views        any  Ready-made views in a Views menu: `[{ id, name, sort, filters, search, columns, groupBy, pageSize }]`; they can't be changed or deleted
  bindViews    statekey  State key for the views people save from the Views menu (the same shape as `views`)
  bindCurrentView statekey  State key holding the id of the view shown (or null); the table opens with it
  defaultView  string  The view the table opens with when `bindCurrentView` has none
  editable     any  Which rows' cells can be edited (in columns with `edit`): true (default), or an expression over `row`, e.g. `{{ row.status != 'Closed' }}`
  addRow       any  Editable: a button under the rows that adds one: `true`, or its text. Rows pasted past the end are added too
  newRow       any  Editable: what an added row starts with, e.g. `{ status: Draft }`
  deletable    bool  Editable: Delete in the bulk bar removes the selected rows (turns on `selectable`)
  errors       any  Editable: messages to mark cells with, e.g. from the server: `{ rowKey: { field: message } }`
  bindErrors   statekey  Editable: state key that gets the cells that are wrong, `[{ key, field, message }]`
  bindChanges  statekey  Editable: state key that gets what changed, `{ rowKey: { field: value } }` (null for a deleted row); set it to `{}` once saved
  id           any  Element id (default: derived from the document)
  parts: toolbar, table, footer
  children: yes
ui-data-table-column: A column of the `ui-data-table` it is in. Children, if any, draw each cell, with the row as `row` and its position as `rowIndex`.
  field        string  The row field shown, sorted and filtered, e.g. `amount` or `customer.name`
  label        any  Header text (default: the field)
  sortable     bool  Click the header to sort (default: when it has a `field` or `sortField`)
  sortField    string  Sort by this field instead, e.g. a rank behind a label (default: `field`)
  filter       one of: text, select, range, date  A filter control in the toolbar (`date`: a range calendar with presets)
  options      any  A `select` filter's choices (default: the column's distinct values)
  presets      any  A `date` filter's shortcuts, as `ui-calendar`'s: names such as `lastQuarter`, `yearToDate` or `quarters` (the last four), or `{ label, from, to }`
  fiscalStart  number  A `date` filter's financial year: the month it starts, 1–12; quarters and years follow it
  align        one of: left, center, right  Default: right for numbers, left otherwise
  format       one of: number, currency, percent, date, datetime  How the browser shows the value (in `locale`)
  currency     string  With `format: currency`, e.g. `EUR` (default `USD`)
  decimals     number  Digits after the point for `number`, `currency` and `percent`
  cell         one of: text, badge, progress, sparkline  Draw the value as `badge`, `progress` (0–100) or `sparkline` (needs the chart kit)
  tones        any  With `cell: badge`, a tone per value: `{ Paid: success, Failed: destructive }`
  summary      one of: sum, avg, min, max, count  A footer cell summing (or averaging, …) the rows that pass the filters
  width        any  Column width
  pin          one of: left, right  Keep the column in view while the table scrolls sideways
  tree         bool  The column that shows nesting: indented, with the arrow that opens a row (default: the first)
  hideable     bool  Listed in the View menu (default true)
  hidden       bool  Starts hidden
  group        any  A header over this column and the ones next to it with the same `group`
  groupable    bool  Offered in the View menu's Group by
  resizable    bool  With the table's `resizable`, false keeps this column's width
  edit         one of: text, multiline, number, date, select, checkbox  Its cells can be edited in place; `select` picks from `options` (default: the column's values)
  required     bool  With `edit`: an empty cell is marked wrong
  min          any  With `edit`: the smallest number, or the first date
  max          any  With `edit`: the largest number, or the last date
  pattern      string  With `edit`: a regular expression the whole text must match
  unique       bool  With `edit`: a value used by another row is marked wrong
  message      any  With `edit`: what's said when `min`, `max` or `pattern` isn't met
  id           string  The column's key when it has no field (default: its position)
  children: yes
ui-data-table-toolbar: Controls added to the table's toolbar, after its filters (e.g. an Add or Export button).
  children: yes
ui-data-table-bulk: Actions shown while rows are selected, next to the count. Read the selection from the table's `bindSelection` key.
  children: yes
ui-data-table-detail: A row's details, shown under it when its expander is opened; the row is in scope as `row`.
  children: yes
ui-chart: A chart drawn by Apache ECharts, from rows (`type`, `data`, `x`, `y`) or a full ECharts `option`.
  type         one of: line, area, bar, scatter, effectScatter, pictorialBar, candlestick, boxplot, pie, donut, funnel, radar, heatmap, gauge, tree, treemap, sunburst, sankey, graph, chord, themeRiver, parallel, gantt, pareto  Series type the shorthand builds; leave it out to use `option` alone
  data         any  Rows (objects or arrays), numbers, or a tree / node list, depending on `type`
  x            any  Field (or column) for categories, names or the x value; default the first
  y            any  Field(s) for values: a field, or a list of fields or `{ field, name, …series options }`; default every other numeric field
  value        any  Third field: heatmap cell value, scatter bubble size
  links        any  `{ source, target, value }` for sankey, graph and chord
  option       any  An ECharts option, merged over what the shorthand builds. `{{ }}` works inside it
  filter       any  Keep rows whose fields match: `{ region: "{{ region }}", date: { from, to }, product: [a, b] }`; blank conditions pass
  aggregate    one of: sum, avg, min, max, count  Group rows by `x` (and `series`)
  series       any  Field whose values become separate series (long-format rows)
  sort         any  A field, `-field` for descending, or a list of them; with `series`, orders the categories by their totals
  limit        any  Keep the first N rows after sorting; with `series`, the first N categories; a pareto adds up the rest into one Other bar
  drill        any  Fields to drill through on click, e.g. `[region, country, city]`
  xType        one of: category, time, value, log  The x axis; default: time for dates on lines and points
  zoom         any  Zoom controls along the category or time axis: `inside`, `slider` or `both` (`true`)
  brush        any  Drag to select: `rect` (`true`), `polygon`, `lineX` or `lineY`
  live         any  Live data: `{ url, every, mode: append, window, key, params, paused, stream, pick, into, status }`
  columns      any  Gantt: the table's columns, a field or `{ field, name, width, align }`; the first holds the tree of names (default `[name]`)
  markers      any  Gantt: dated lines down the timeline, `[{ at, name, color }]`
  today        bool  Gantt: a line at today's date when it's on the timeline (default true)
  bindData     statekey  Gantt: the state key `data` reads; bars dragged (or moved with Alt and the arrows) write their new dates back to it
  editable     bool  Gantt: with `bindData`, bars can be moved and stretched, and links drawn and removed (default true)
  visibleRows  number  Gantt: at most this many rows tall; the rest scroll inside the chart, under its dates and beside its table
  workdays     any  Gantt: count and move whole-day tasks on working days, days off shaded: `true` for Monday to Friday, or the weekdays that work (0 is Sunday), e.g. `[0, 1, 2, 3, 4]`
  holidays     any  Gantt: dates that aren't working days either, with `workdays`, e.g. `["2026-12-25"]`
  critical     bool  Gantt: mark the critical path, the tasks with no slack whose delay would move the plan's end (ringed, their links in red)
  baselines    bool  Gantt: draw each task's `baselineStart` and `baselineEnd` (its planned dates) as a thin bar under it, with how late or early it is (default true)
  snap         any  Gantt: the step a task with times of day moves and stretches by, in minutes or as `"15m"`, `"1h"` or `"1d"` (default a day); tasks in whole days move by days
  cascade      any  Gantt: moving or stretching a task moves on the tasks that wait on it, so they start after it ends; `"both"` also pulls them back to start when it ends
  threshold    any  Pareto: a dashed line at this cumulative percent, the bars past it faded (default 80; `false` for none)
  stack        bool  Stack the series
  smooth       bool  Smooth lines
  horizontal   bool  Bars along the x axis
  labels       bool  Show value labels on the marks
  format       one of: number, currency, percent  How values show in labels, tooltips and the value axis, in the document's language
  currency     string  With `format: currency`, e.g. `EUR` (default `USD`)
  decimals     number  Digits after the point in labels and tooltips (default: up to 2)
  legend       bool  Show the legend (default: with two or more series)
  tooltip      bool  Show a tooltip on hover (default true)
  height       any  Number (px) or CSS length; default 320
  renderer     one of: canvas, svg  Overrides the kit's renderer
  loading      any  Show the loading mask, e.g. `{{ fetching }}`
  bind         statekey  Two-way: the clicked item's name; clicking it again clears it
  bindRow      statekey  The clicked item's row; clicking it again clears it
  bindZoom     statekey  Two-way: the zoom window as `{ from, to }` axis values, or null
  bindLegend   statekey  Two-way: the names of the visible series
  bindBrush    statekey  The rows inside the brushed area
  bindDrill    statekey  Two-way: the drill path, e.g. `[Europe, Germany]`
  maps         any  GeoJSON maps to register first: `{ world: /geo/world.json }`
  group        string  Charts in the same group share tooltips and zoom
  title        any  Accessible name, read before the generated description
  children: no
ui-sparkline: A small chart without axes, for a trend inside text or a stat card.
  data         any (required)  Numbers, or rows with `y`
  y            any  Field holding the value, when `data` has rows
  type         one of: line, area, bar  Default `area`
  height       any  Number (px) or CSS length; default 40
  width        any  Number (px) or CSS length; default 100%
  tooltip      bool  Show the value on hover (default true)
  option       any  An ECharts option, merged over the sparkline's
  live         any  Live data, as for `ui-chart`
  children: no
ui-live-data: Keeps a state key filled from a polled URL, server-sent events or a WebSocket, for any component to read.
  url          any (required)  Polled with GET, or a `ws://` / `wss://` WebSocket; may use state
  into         statekey (required)  State key that holds the data
  every        any  Milliseconds between polls (default 5000, at least 250)
  mode         one of: replace, append  Replace the data with each message (default), or append to it
  window       any  With `append`: keep the last N rows (default 500)
  key          any  With `append`: a row with the same value in this field replaces the old one
  params       any  Query parameters; blank ones are left out, and a change reconnects
  paused       any  Stop while true, e.g. `{{ !liveMode }}`
  stream       bool  Listen to `url` as server-sent events instead of polling
  pick         string  Path to the data in each message, e.g. `data.items`
  status       statekey  State key set to connecting, live, paused or error
  children: no
ui-flow: A diagram of nodes and edges in React Flow's JSON shape. Node and edge types are `ui-flow-node` / `ui-flow-edge` children; `ui-flow-panel` children float above it.
  nodes        any (required)  Nodes as React Flow saves them: `{ id, type, position: { x, y }, data, parentId, width, height, className, style, hidden }`
  edges        any  Edges: `{ id, source, target, sourceHandle, targetHandle, type, label, animated, markerEnd, markerStart, className, style, hidden }`
  layout       any  `layered` places the top-level nodes automatically, ignoring their positions; default: use `position`
  direction    any  `LR` (default), `TB`, `RL` or `BT`: the layout's direction, and where ports without a `side` go
  nodeGap      any  Layout: space between nodes in a rank (default 40)
  rankGap      any  Layout: space between ranks (default 80)
  nodeOrigin   any  Which point of a node `position` names, as fractions: `[0, 0]` top left (default), `[0.5, 0]` top centre
  edgePath     any  Path for edges whose type and template don't name one: `bezier` (default), `straight`, `step` or `smoothstep`
  fit          any  Fit the view to the nodes when they first appear (default true)
  fitPadding   any  Space left around the nodes when fitting, as a fraction of the view (default 0.1)
  viewport     any  The view to start at when `fit` is false: `{ x, y, zoom }`
  center       any  A node id: the view pans to that node whenever this changes
  highlight    any  `neighbors`: while a node is selected, dim everything not connected to it
  selectable   any  Click or Enter selects a node or edge; Shift adds to the selection (default true)
  editable     any  Turns on `draggable`, `connectable` and `deletable` together (default false)
  draggable    any  Nodes can be dragged (default: `editable`)
  connectable  any  Drag from a port to another to connect them; needs `bindEdges` (default: `editable`)
  deletable    any  Delete or Backspace removes the selection; needs `bindNodes` / `bindEdges` (default: `editable`)
  connect      any  Connection rules: `{ sameParent, self, unique, pairs: [{ source, target }] }` (node types)
  newEdge      any  Fields every new edge starts with, e.g. `{ type: smoothstep, markerEnd: arrowclosed }`
  newNode      any  A node (`{ type, data }`) made where a connection is dropped on empty canvas, and joined to it
  confirmDelete any  The id of a dialog to open before deleting; its button sends `flow.delete`
  pan          any  Drag the background to pan (default true)
  zoom         any  Wheel, pinch and keys zoom (default true)
  wheel        any  What the wheel does: `zoom` (default) or `pan` (Ctrl/⌘ + wheel zooms)
  minZoom      any  Default 0.1
  maxZoom      any  Default 2
  background   one of: dots, lines, none  Background pattern (default dots)
  controls     bool  Zoom and fit buttons (default true)
  minimap      bool  An overview in the corner that pans the view (default false)
  height       any  Number (px) or CSS length; default 480. The width is the container's
  title        any  Accessible name
  bind         statekey  State key holding the selected node's id (null when none)
  bindNodes    statekey  State key that gets the nodes, with new positions, after a drag
  bindViewport statekey  State key kept in sync with the view: `{ x, y, zoom }`
  nodeStyles   any  Apply each node's saved `style` and `className` (default true). Turn off when the template works the look out from `data`
  filter       any  Node ids to show; the rest are hidden, except the nodes they connect to, shown as context (`data-neighbor`). Empty or null shows all
  filterNeighbors any  With `filter`, also show the nodes the shown ones connect to (default true)
  search       any  Text to find in the nodes: matches are marked `data-match`, everything else is dimmed
  bindMatches  statekey  State key holding the ids of the nodes `search` matches
  bindHistory  statekey  State key holding how many edits can be undone and redone: `{ undo, redo }`
  bindEdges    statekey  State key that gets the edges after a connection or a deletion
  bindNode     statekey  State key holding the selected node itself (its `id`, `type`, `data`, …), or null: for a side panel that shows or edits it
  bindSelection statekey  State key holding every selected node and edge: `{ nodes: [ids], edges: [ids] }`
  bindDelete   statekey  With `confirmDelete`: what would be deleted, `{ nodes, edges }`, while the dialog is open
  parts: controls, minimap
  children: yes
ui-flow-node: A node type of the `ui-flow` it is in: its children are drawn for every node of that `type`, with the node in scope as `node`. Place `ui-flow-port`s inside.
  type         string  The node type this template draws. Leave it out (or use `default`) for every type no other template declares
  variant      one of: card, plain  `card` (default) gives the node a border, background and padding; `plain` leaves all of it to `style`
  shape        any  The node's outline: `rect`, `rounded`, `pill`, `circle`, `ellipse`, `diamond`, `hexagon`, `parallelogram`, `triangle` or `cylinder`; or `polygon` with `points`. May use the node, e.g. `{{ node.data.shape }}`. Style it through `parts.shape` (`fill`, `stroke`)
  points       any  With `shape: polygon`: the corners as percentages of the box, e.g. `50,0 100,50 50,100 0,50`
  container    bool  Other nodes can sit inside it: dragging a node onto it makes it the node's parent, and off it, takes it out
  resizable    bool  A handle in the bottom-right corner resizes the node; the size is saved as its `width` and `height`
  minWidth     number  Smallest width when resizing (default 80)
  minHeight    number  Smallest height when resizing (default 40)
  parts: shape
  children: yes
ui-flow-edge: An edge type of the `ui-flow` it is in. Its `style` styles the path (`stroke`, `stroke-width`, …); its children, with the edge in scope as `edge`, are the label. Without children the label is `edge.label`.
  type         string  The edge type this template draws. Leave it out (or use `default`) for every type no other template declares
  path         one of: bezier, straight, step, smoothstep  Path shape; default: the edge's own type when it is one of these, else the flow's `edgePath`
  marker       one of: none, arrow, arrowclosed  Arrowhead at the target, unless the edge has `markerEnd`
  markerStart  one of: none, arrow, arrowclosed  Arrowhead at the source, unless the edge has `markerStart`
  animated     bool  Moving dashes, unless the edge sets `animated`
  floating     bool  Attach to the nodes' borders, facing each other, instead of to ports
  parts: label
  children: yes
ui-flow-port: Where edges attach to a node, in a `ui-flow-node`. It is placed on its side of the nearest positioned element: the node, or e.g. a table row with `position: relative`.
  id           any  The port's id, matched against an edge's `sourceHandle` / `targetHandle`. May use the node, e.g. `{{ c.handle }}`
  type         one of: source, target  Edges leave from `source` ports (default) and arrive at `target` ports
  side         any  `left`, `right`, `top` or `bottom`. Default: from the flow's `direction`, e.g. targets left and sources right for `LR`
  offset       any  Where along the side, e.g. `30%` or `24px`. Default: ports on one side share it evenly
  accepts      any  Node types allowed at the other end of a new connection, e.g. `[step, merge]`
  max          any  How many edges this port takes at most
  scope        one of: children  `children`: connects only to nodes inside this node (a container), whatever `sameParent` says
  connectable  any  Whether new connections can start or end here (default true)
  children: no
ui-flow-panel: Content that floats above a `ui-flow`, e.g. a toolbar. It doesn't pan or zoom.
  position     one of: top-left, top-center, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-center, bottom-right  Corner or edge of the flow (default top-left)
  children: yes
ui-flow-item: A palette entry: drag it onto a `ui-flow` to add its `node` there, or click it to add the node in the middle of the view. The flow needs `bindNodes`.
  node         any (required)  The node to add: `{ type, data }`, and `id` if it should keep one
  flow         string  The element id of the flow to add to. Default: the flow it is in, or the page's only flow
  children: yes
ui-map: A map, on OpenStreetMap or Google Maps, with markers, popups, shapes, clusters and picking a place. A `ui-map-popup` child is the popup's content; `ui-map-panel` children float above it.
  provider     one of: osm, google  `osm` (default): OpenStreetMap, no key needed. `google`: Google Maps, which needs an API key
  markers      any  Places, as rows: `{ id, lat, lng, title, description, label, tone, color, alarm, effect, href, draggable }`, usually from data or state. `label` is a letter, number or emoji in the pin
  latField     string  The rows' latitude field (default `lat`, else `latitude`)
  lngField     string  The rows' longitude field (default `lng`, else `lon`, `long` or `longitude`)
  titleField   string  The rows' title field (default `title`, else `name`)
  toneBy       any  Colours markers by a field: `{ field: status, tones: { late: danger, done: success } }`
  alarmBy      any  Which markers are in alarm: `{ field: status, values: [offline, fault] }`, or `alarm: true` on a row. They pulse in red with a `!`, stay on top, and a new one is announced
  effectBy     any  Animates markers by a field: `{ field: status, effects: { late: glow } }`, or `effect` on a row: `pulse`, `glow`, `bounce` or `blink`. Still, where the viewer asked for less motion
  filter       any  Shows only the markers that pass: `{ field: condition }`, as `ui-data-table`'s and `ui-chart`'s `filter`, e.g. a `ui-filters` panel's `bind`
  shapes       any  Lines, areas and circles: `{ id, type: line | area | circle, points: [[lat, lng], …], center, radius (metres), title, tone, color, width, dashed, fill }`
  geojson      any  GeoJSON lines and areas, styled by each feature's `properties` (`tone`, `color`, `width`, `title`); its points become markers
  overlays     any  Layers over the map: `{ id, type: image, url, bounds: [[south, west], [north, east]] }`, e.g. a floor plan; `{ type: tiles, url, attribution }`, e.g. sea marks; `{ type: heat, points, weightField, radius, max }`. Each with `opacity` and `show`, which may use state
  center       any  `[lat, lng]` or `{ lat, lng }`. The map moves when it changes. Default: fitted to what's on it
  zoom         any  0 (the world) to 19 (a building); default 13 with a `center`
  minZoom      number  How far out it zooms
  maxZoom      number  How far in it zooms, and the closest it fits to
  fit          any  Fits the view to the markers and shapes when it opens (default: without a `center`); `always`: whenever they change
  cluster      any  Groups markers closer than this many px (`true`: 56), with how many there are; clicking a group zooms to it
  bind         statekey  State key with the selected marker's id (null when none). Setting it selects that marker and brings it into view
  bindMarker   statekey  State key with the selected marker itself, or null
  bindShape    statekey  State key with the id of the shape last clicked; shapes are clickable with it
  bindView     statekey  State key kept at `{ center, zoom, bounds: { north, south, east, west } }`
  bindVisible  statekey  State key with the ids of the markers in view, e.g. for a list beside the map
  bindAlarms   statekey  State key with the ids of the markers in alarm, e.g. for a count
  bindPoint    statekey  Picks a place: clicking the map puts a pin there, which can be dragged, and writes `{ lat, lng }`
  bindMarkers  statekey  State key the rows are in: a dragged marker's new place is written back to its row
  bindLocation statekey  State key that gets `{ lat, lng, accuracy }` after My location
  draggable    any  Markers can be dragged, or moved with Alt and the arrow keys (needs `bindMarkers`)
  popup        bool  Opens a popup over the selected marker, with its title and description or the `ui-map-popup` (default true)
  locate       bool  A My location button: shows where the viewer is, once they allow it
  controls     bool  Zoom and fit buttons (default true)
  gestures     one of: cooperative, greedy, none  `cooperative` (default): the page scrolls past the map, and Ctrl / ⌘ + wheel or two fingers zoom it. `greedy`: the map takes the wheel and one finger. `none`: it stays put
  tiles        any  With `osm`, another tile server: `{ url, attribution, attributionUrl, maxZoom, darkUrl }`, `url` having `{z}`, `{x}` and `{y}`
  darkTiles    bool  With `osm`, darken the tiles in dark mode when there's no `darkUrl` (default true)
  apiKey       any  With `google`, the API key (default: the one the host set). Browsers see it, so restrict it to your sites
  mapId        any  With `google`, a map id from Google's console, for its cloud styles
  mapType      one of: roadmap, satellite, hybrid, terrain  With `google` (default `roadmap`)
  height       any  Number (px) or CSS length; default 400. The width is the container's
  title        any  Names the map for screen readers (default `Map`)
  parts: controls
  children: yes
ui-map-popup: What a `ui-map`'s popup shows, with the selected marker in scope as `marker`.
  children: yes
ui-map-panel: Content that floats above a `ui-map`, e.g. a legend or a search box. It doesn't move with the map.
  position     one of: top-left, top-center, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-center, bottom-right  Corner or edge of the map (default top-left)
  children: yes
ui-twin: A digital twin: a 3D world drawn with three.js from models of most formats, every part of it configurable and able to use state, with machine and sensor values shown on the objects, alarms, paths things follow, zones, views and editing the layout. A `ui-twin-popup` child is the popup's content; `ui-twin-panel` children float above it.
  models       any  The models by name: `{ forklift: models/forklift.glb, pump: { url, scale, units: m | cm | mm | in | ft, up: y | z, rotate, fit, origin: base | center | none, format, mtl, color } }`. glTF / GLB (with Draco, meshopt and KTX2), OBJ (with `mtl`), FBX, STL, PLY, DAE, 3MF, 3DS, WRL and USD / USDZ. `fit`: the largest side in metres, or `[w, h, d]` to fit in. Each is made to stand on the ground at its middle unless `origin` says otherwise. `far`: how it's drawn far from the camera, a simpler model's url, `{ url, distance }`, `{ ratio, distance }` (made simpler in the browser, `ratio` of its triangles) or `false` (see `lod`)
  objects      any  What's in the world, as rows: `{ id, model | shape: box | cylinder | sphere | cone | sensor | point, size, color, position: [x, z] | [x, y, z], rotation (degrees, or [x, y, z]), scale, title, description, label, tone, alarm, effect, path, speed, progress, loop, face, attach, animation, opacity, clickable, href, … }`, in metres with y up. Any other fields are the object's data (a machine's speed, a sensor's value): `readouts` show them. Usually from data or state, so they move when it changes
  readouts     any  Values shown on the objects that have them: `[{ field, label, unit, decimals, warn, alarm, below, tag, when, models, history }]`. Past `warn` an object turns warning, past `alarm` it's in alarm (`below: true`: under them); `when` (a `filter`) or `models` limit a readout to some objects, so each kind can have its own limits. The first two are on its tag (`tag` says otherwise); all are in its popup. `history: n` keeps an object's last n values (a point each time it changes, up to 500) and draws them as a sparkline in its popup
  colorBy      any  Colours objects by a value: `{ field, min, max, colors: [blue, green, yellow, red] }`, e.g. temperatures
  live         any  Machine and sensor values from a feed of the twin's own: `{ url, every: 5000 }` polled, or `{ stream: url }` (server-sent events). Each answer is rows with an `id`, or `{ <id>: { field: value } }`, merged into the objects with that id
  paths        any  Routes: `{ id, points: [[x, z], …], closed, width, tone, color, flow, height, show }`. `flow: true` (or a speed) moves stripes along it; an object with `path` follows it at `speed` m/s (default 1), or stands at `progress` (0 to 1)
  zones        any  Areas on the ground: `{ id, points: [[x, z], …] | center: [x, z] and size: [w, d], tone, color, label, title, description, height, opacity }`. With `bindZone` or a `title` they can be clicked
  walls        any  Walls: `{ points: [[x, z], …], closed, height (default 3), thickness (default 0.2), color, opacity }`
  ground       any  `{ size: [w, d], center, color, grid: 1 (metres a cell) | false }`, or false for none. Default: big enough for everything, with a 1 m grid
  environment  any  `{ preset: studio | day | night, light (default 1), shadows (default true), background, fog }`
  camera       any  `{ position: [x, y, z], target: [x, y, z], fov }`. The camera moves there when it changes. Default: fitted to the world
  views        any  Named views, shown as buttons: `[{ id, label, position, target }]`
  world        any  All of the above in one object (`{ models, objects, paths, zones, walls, ground, environment, camera, views, readouts, colorBy }`), e.g. a layout kept in state; a prop of its own wins
  src          any  The address of such a world as JSON, fetched in the browser
  follow       any  The id of an object the camera follows, keeping its distance
  filter       any  Shows only the objects that pass: `{ field: condition }`, as `ui-data-table`'s and `ui-chart`'s `filter`, e.g. a `ui-filters` panel's `bind`
  toneBy       any  Tones objects by a field: `{ field: status, tones: { running: success, idle: neutral, fault: danger } }`; a ring in it is drawn under each
  alarmBy      any  Which objects are in alarm: `{ field: status, values: [fault] }`, or `alarm: true` on a row, or a readout past `alarm`. They glow red, get a `!` tag, and a new one is announced
  effectBy     any  Animates objects by a field: `{ field: state, effects: { running: spin } }`, or `effect` on a row: `pulse`, `glow`, `blink`, `spin` (`spin`: degrees a second) or `bob`. Still, where the viewer asked for less motion
  labels       one of: auto, all, none  Tags over objects: `auto` (default) for those with a `label`, readouts or an alarm; `all`; `none` (alarms still)
  editable     any  Objects can be dragged on the ground, or moved with Alt and the arrow keys and turned with Alt+R (needs `bindObjects`)
  multiple     bool  Several objects picked at once: ⌘, Ctrl or Shift and a click adds or takes one away (on the view, a tag or the list), Shift and a drag from the floor draws a box around more, ⌘A picks them all. Editable, they're dragged, moved, turned and removed together. The last one picked is the selected one (`bind`); all are in `bindSelected`
  snap         any  Metres moves snap to, e.g. 0.5
  measure      any  A ruler button among the controls (or M with the view focused): two clicks, on objects, walls or the floor, and the distance between them is drawn and said, with how far across and how far up when both count. Picked from a tag or the list, an object counts from its middle on the floor. Escape stops
  palette      any  While `editable`, things to add, as rows like `objects` without a place: `[{ label, model | shape, title, … }]`. Clicked, one is added in the middle of the view; dragged into it, where it's dropped. Delete removes the selected object
  bind         statekey  State key with the selected object's id (null when none). Setting it selects that object and brings it into view
  bindObject   statekey  State key with the selected object itself, with its latest values
  bindSelected statekey  State key with the ids of the objects picked (with `multiple`, several; else the selected one's); setting it picks them
  bindZone     statekey  State key with the id of the zone last clicked
  bindView     statekey  State key with the current view's id; setting it moves the camera there
  bindAlarms   statekey  State key with the ids of the objects in alarm, e.g. for a count
  bindObjects  statekey  State key the objects are in: a moved one's `position` and `rotation` are written back to its row
  bindLive     statekey  State key that gets the latest values from `live`, as `{ <id>: { field: value } }`, e.g. for a list or totals beside the twin
  bindMeasure  statekey  State key with the last measurement, `{ from, to, distance, across, up }` in metres (null when none)
  bindCamera   statekey  State key kept at `{ position, target }` after the camera's moved, e.g. to copy into `views`
  popup        bool  Opens a popup over the selected object, with its title, description and readouts or the `ui-twin-popup` (default true)
  controls     bool  Zoom and fit buttons (default true)
  gestures     one of: orbit, none  `orbit` (default): drag to turn, right-drag or two fingers to move, wheel or pinch to zoom. `none`: the camera stays put
  transition   number  Milliseconds an object takes to move to a new place from the data (default 600; 0 jumps)
  quality      one of: high, low  `low`: no shadows or smoothing, for big worlds or slow devices
  lod          any  Models drawn simpler far from the camera: `auto` (default) for a model used by 100 objects or more, `true` for every model, `false` (or `none`) for none, or `{ ratio, distance }` (default 0.15 of the triangles, past twelve times the model's size and at least 15 m) for every model. Made in the browser with meshoptimizer's simplifier; a model's own `far` wins. Only for objects drawn together (not those in a look of their own)
  motionScale  number  While the camera moves, the view is drawn at this share of its resolution each way (default 0.65), and sharp again 400 ms after it stops; 1 keeps it sharp
  height       any  Number (px) or CSS length; default 480. The width is the container's
  title        any  Names the view for screen readers (default `3D view`)
  parts: controls
  children: yes
ui-twin-popup: What a `ui-twin`'s popup shows, with the selected object (and its latest values) in scope as `object`.
  children: yes
ui-twin-panel: Content that floats above a `ui-twin`, e.g. a legend, counts or filters. It doesn't move with the camera.
  position     one of: top-left, top-center, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-center, bottom-right  Corner or edge of the view (default top-left)
  children: yes
ui-icon: An SVG icon from the icon kit's packs, drawn in the current text colour.
  name         string (required)  `pack:icon` (e.g. `logistics:truck`) or a bare `icon`, found in the first pack that has it
  variant      one of: outline, filled  `outline` (default) or `filled`
  size         any  Number (px) or CSS length; default `1em`, the size of the text around it, times the theme's `size.icon`
  label        any  Accessible name. Without one the icon is decorative and hidden from screen readers
  children: no
```
